zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Aʿrāf
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿المص﴾. We have already explained these letters at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara, but we repeat here something of their explanation because of a point concerning their i'rab (grammatical analysis). What we chose in explaining them is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās: that "الـمـص" means "I am Allah; I know best and I distinguish (أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ وأفْصِلُ)". One of the grammarians said: the position of these letters is nominative by virtue of what follows them. He said: ﴿المص﴾ ﴿كِتابٌ﴾ — "كِتابٌ" is put in the nominative by "الـمـص", as though its meaning were: "الـمـص are the letters of a Book sent down to you". Were it as he described, the mention of the Book would always come after these letters. Yet His saying ﴿الم﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 1] ﴿اللَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا هُوَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 2] shows that "الـم" has nothing to put it in the nominative on his view; likewise ﴿يس﴾ [Yā Sīn: 1] ﴿والقُرْآنِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 2], and likewise ﴿حم﴾ [al-Shūrā: 1] ﴿عسق﴾ [al-Shūrā: 2] ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي إلَيْكَ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 3].
And His saying: ﴿حم﴾ [al-Dukhān: 1] ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 2] ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 3] — these things show that the matter is otherwise than he stated. Moreover, were it so, "الـم" would not be repeated, nor "حـم" repeated.
The grammarians are agreed that His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿كِتابٌ أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ﴾ is put in the nominative by something other than these letters, the meaning being: "This is a Book sent down to you (هَذا كِتابٌ أُنْزِلَ إلَيْكَ)". And he agrees with them that what they said is permissible, so they must be followed, since both his view and theirs [accept it], and whoever holds this view is obliged to establish proof for differing from them. Moreover, were it as he describes, he would be implying two nouns, so that the meaning would be: "الـمص are some of the letters of a Book sent down to you", and he would thus have implied the muḍāf (first term of the genitive construct) and what it is annexed to, and this is not permissible.
If someone says: one may say "ألِفْ با تا ثا are twenty-eight letters", though you have mentioned only four — so how is that permissible? It is answered: "ألِفْ با تا ثا" has become the name of these [letters], just as you say: "اَلْحَمْدُ is seven verses", where "اَلْحَمْدُ" is a name for the whole sūra; but "الـم" is not the name of the Book, nor is "طـسـم" the name of the Qurʾān, and this is a clear difference. These letters, as we have described, are letters of the alphabet, indeclinable (mabnī) on the pause, and they stand in the place of clauses; and a clause — when it is only a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) — has no grammatical position. So if the meaning of "كهيعص" is: the kāf means "كافٍ (sufficient)", the hāʾ means "هادٍ (guide)", the yāʾ and the ʿayn are from "عَلِيمٌ (all-knowing)", and the ṣād is from "صَدُوقٌ (truthful)", and the meaning of "الـم" is "أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ (I am Allah, I know best)", then their position is only like the position of the thing that is their interpretation; and there is no position in i'rab for your saying "أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ", nor for your saying "هو هادٍ" and "هو كافٍ": some of this is put in the nominative by the rest, and the clause has no position.
And His saying: ﴿فَلا يَكُنْ في صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِنهُ﴾ — the meaning of "اَلْحَرَجُ" is tightness (اَلضِّيقُ). There are two interpretations of it. One is that it means: "Let your breast not be straitened by conveying [the message], and do not fear", because it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "My Lord, I fear that they will smash my head and make it like a loaf of bread", so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — informed him that he was safe from them, and said: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67], and said: ﴿فَلا يَكُنْ في صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِنهُ﴾, that is: let your breast not be straitened by delivering what you have been sent with. It was also said: "Do not doubt it at all (فَلا تَشُكَّنَّ فِيهِ)". Both explanations are valid. As for the interpretation "do not doubt", and the interpretation of ﴿فَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ المُمْتَرِينَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 114], and the interpretation of ﴿فَإنْ كُنْتَ في شَكٍّ مِمّا أنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكَ فاسْألِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ [Yūnus: 94]: what he ﷺ was addressed with is an address to his community, so it is as though it were "do not doubt (plural) and do not be uncertain (فَلا تَشُكُّوا ولا تَرْتابُوا)".
And His saying: ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ بِهِ﴾ — its sense is that of being placed earlier [in the order]; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "A Book sent down to you that you may warn by it, and a reminder to the believers; so let there be no tightness in your breast from it". And "ذِكْرى" may be in the position of nominative, accusative or genitive. The accusative is on the reading: "sent down that you may warn by it, and as a reminder to the believers", i.e. "and that you may remind by it with a reminding (ولِتُذَكِّرَ بِهِ ذِكْرى)", because warning contains the sense of reminding.
It may also be "and it is a reminder to the believers (وهو ذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ)", like your saying "and it is a remembrance for the believers (وهو ذِكْرٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ)". The genitive is on the sense of "لِتُنْذِرَ", because the meaning of "لِتُنْذِرَ" is "لِأنْ تُنْذِرَ (in order that you warn)", so it is in the position of the genitive, the meaning being: for warning and for reminding. As for "ذِكْرى", it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) containing the feminine alif, like "دَعَوْتُ دَعْوى", and like "رَجَعْتُهُ رُجْعى" and "اِتَّقَيْتُ تَقْوى", except that it is a noun standing in the place of the maṣdar.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
And His saying: ﴿اتَّبِعُوا ما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكم مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: follow the Qurʾān and what has come from the Prophet ﷺ, because it is part of what was sent down to him, by His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وما نَهاكم عَنْهُ فانْتَهُوا﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7].
﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ﴾, that is: do not take as allies those who have turned away from the religion of truth, and whoever has approved of one of the [false] doctrines; for the believer is the ally of the believer: ﴿والمُؤْمِنُونَ والمُؤْمِناتُ بَعْضُهم أوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Tawba: 71]. And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قَلِيلا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: "ما" is redundant (zāʾida) and emphatic; the meaning is: "قَلِيلًا تَذَكَّرُونَ (little do you take heed)". In "تَذَكَّرُونَ" there are two readings: "قَلِيلًا ما تَذَّكَّرُونَ" with a doubled dhāl, the meaning being "قَلِيلًا ما تَتَذَكَّرُونَ", except that the tāʾ is assimilated into the dhāl because the place [of articulation] of the one is near that of the other. And whoever reads "تَذَكَّرُونَ", the original is also "تَتَذَكَّرُونَ", except that he has dropped one of the two tāʾs, namely the second, because both are augments; but the first indicates the sense of the future, so it may not be dropped, while the second entered only with the sense of "I did the thing gradually", as in "تَفَهَّمْتُ" and "تَعَلَّمْتُ", i.e. "I brought the thing about by degrees"; and it also enters with the sense of displaying something while the reality is otherwise, as in your saying "تَقَيَّسْتُ", i.e. I made out that I was of Qays. So what is dropped from "تَتَفَعَّلُونَ" is the second [tāʾ], because what remains in the word — the doubling of the ʿayn of "تَفَعَّلَ" — indicates the meaning of the word; whereas if the tāʾ of the future were dropped, the sense of the future would be lost.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَكَمْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ أهْلَكْناها﴾: the meaning is: How many people of a town have We destroyed! But "أهْلِ" has been omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech.
And His saying: ﴿فَجاءَها بَأْسُنا بَياتًا﴾ is construed according to the wording of "القَرْيَةِ"; had it been said "فَجاءَهم", it would have been correct.
And His saying: ﴿أوْ هم قائِلُونَ﴾: one of the grammarians said: the meaning is "وَهم قائِلُونَ (while they were taking their midday rest)", and the wāw, as he mentioned, is omitted. But this does not require implying the wāw: if you said "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ راجِلًا، أوْ وهو فارِسٌ (Zayd came to me on foot, or while he was riding)", or "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ هو فارِسٌ (Zayd came to me, he riding)", you would not need a wāw, because the reference [pronoun] has returned to the first. The meaning of "بَياتًا" is: by night. One says "باتَ بَياتًا حَسَنًا" and "بِيتَةً حَسَنَةً (he spent a good night)", and the maṣdar (verbal noun) in [the sense of] night raids is "بَيْتًا". And "اَلْبَيْتُ" is the tent of hair, and likewise the house of clay; the origin of its name is only that it is suitable for spending the night. One says: "So-and-so has a بِيتَة and a night's [provision]" and "بَيْتُ لَيْلَةٍ", i.e. enough food to suffice him for a night. The meaning of "أوْ هم قائِلُونَ" is: "or Our might came upon them by day at the time of the midday rest (القائِلَة)". One says "قِلْتُ (I took the midday rest)" from "اَلْقائِلَةُ". So the meaning is: "Our might came upon them unawares, while they were not expecting it, either by night while they were asleep, or by day while they were taking their midday rest", as though they were heedless. And "أوْ" has entered here in the sense of the thing varying and occurring, now this way and now that way; so in this statement it is like "أوْ" of permission (al-ibāḥa). You say "جالِسْ زَيْدًا أوْ عَمْرًا (sit with Zayd or ʿAmr)", i.e. "each of them is worthy of being sat with". And "أوْ" here is better than the wāw, because the wāw implies the two things being together: if you said "ضَرَبْتُ القَوْمَ قِيامًا وقُعُودًا (I struck the people standing and sitting)", the wāw would entail that you struck them while they were in both these states; but if you say "ضَرَبْتُهم قِيامًا أوْ ضَرَبْتُهم قُعُودًا (I struck them standing or I struck them sitting)", without being in doubt, the meaning is only that you struck them once in this state and once in that state. The position of "كَمْ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "أهْلَكْناها". This is better than its being in the position of the accusative, because your saying "زَيْدٌ ضَرَبْتُهُ" is better than "زَيْدًا ضَرَبْتُهُ"; yet the accusative is also good, sound Arabic, as in His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 49].

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَما كانَ دَعْواهم إذْ جاءَهم بَأْسُنا إلا أنْ قالُوا إنّا كُنّا ظالِمِينَ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that of the doctrine and religion they used to profess and lay claim to, they came away with nothing but the confession that they had been wrongdoers. "اَلدَّعْوى" is a noun for what one claims; and "اَلدَّعْوى" may also be in the sense of "اَلدُّعاءُ (supplication)": if you said "O Allah, include us in the righteous supplication (دُعاءِ) of the Muslims" and "دَعْوى المُسْلِمِينَ", it would be permissible. Sībawayh related that, and recited:
وَلَّتْ ودَعْواها كَثِيرٌ صَخَبُهْ
(She turned away, and her calling out was loud in its clamour.)
As for the position of "أنْ": it is best that it be nominative and that "الدَّعْوى" be in the position of the accusative, as He — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿ما كانَ حُجَّتَهم إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 25]. It may also be in the position of the accusative, with "الدَّعْوى" in the position of the nominative; but when "الدَّعْوى" is in the nominative position, the more common wording is "فَما كانَتْ دَعْواهم كَذا وكَذا إلّا أنْ...", because "الدَّعْوى" is feminine in form; yet "كانَ دَعْواهُ باطِلًا" and "باطِلَةً" are both permissible.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الحَقُّ فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾. People have differed about the mention of the Balance on the Day of Resurrection. It has come in some exegesis that it is a balance with two pans, and that the balance was sent down to the world so that people would deal with one another justly, and that deeds will be weighed by it. Some said: "اَلْمِيزانُ" is justice, taking it from your saying "this is of the weight of that", even if it is not something that is weighed; its interpretation is that it has stood in the mind as equal to another, just as weight stands in the eye's view. And some said: "اَلْمِيزانُ" is the book in which the deeds of creatures are recorded. All of this is in the domain of language, and arguing [from it] is acceptable; but what is more fitting is to follow what has come with sound chains of transmission (asānīd). If it has come in a report transmitted by trustworthy people that it is a balance with two pans, then that ought to be accepted. It has been related from Jarīr from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that the Balance is justice; and Allah knows best the reality of that. In any case, the whole of the servants' deeds will be weighed with the utmost justice and truth, and that is His saying: ﴿فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾. We have explained "اَلْمُفْلِحُ" previously.

zajjaj:95-95.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنا مَكانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الحَسَنَةَ حَتّى عَفَوْا﴾ means: they became numerous, and their wealth became abundant.
His saying: ﴿قَدْ مَسَّ آباءَنا الضَّرّاءُ والسَّرّاءُ﴾: Allah seized them so that they would take heed and desist from disbelief and from denying the prophets, but they said: "The like of this touched our fathers", that is: it is the ordinary course of time to bring this, and this is no punishment. So Allah made clear that their interpretation was a mistake, when they already knew that nations before them had been destroyed for their disbelief.
His saying: ﴿فَأخَذْناهم بَغْتَةً﴾ means: suddenly, ﴿وَهم لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ (while they did not perceive). This is what Allah the Exalted related about past nations, so that the community of Muhammad ﷺ would take heed. Then He said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ أهْلَ القُرى آمَنُوا واتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 96], that is: rain would have come to them from the sky and vegetation from the earth, and He would have made that thriving and abundant.

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿أفَأمِنَ أهْلُ القُرى أنْ يَأْتِيَهم بَأْسُنا بَياتًا﴾ means: by night; that is: "Does the community that denied the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ feel secure that Our might will come upon them بَياتًا?!", i.e. by night, ﴿وَهم نائِمُونَ﴾ (while they are asleep). One says: "نامَ الرَّجُلُ، يَنامُ، نَوْمًا، فَهو نائِمٌ" (the man slept, sleeps, sleeping, so he is asleep), and "وهو حَسَنُ النِّيمَةِ"; and "رَجُلٌ نُومَةٌ" when he is a lowly man to whom no attention is paid, and "رَجُلٌ نُوَمَةٌ" when he sleeps a great deal; and "فُلانٌ حَسَنُ النِّيمَةِ" means: his manner of sleeping is good; and "اَلنِّيمُ" is a fur garment. And the fāʾ in His saying: "أفَأمِنَ".
[Translator's note: the entry breaks off here; the sentence about the fāʾ continues at the beginning of the next entry (7:98).]

zajjaj:98-98.t:
And the wāw in His saying: "أوَ أمِنَ" were given fatḥa because they are a conjunctive wāw and a conjunctive fāʾ which the interrogative alif has entered upon.
[Translator's note: this sentence continues the end of the previous entry (7:97), which mentions the fāʾ in "أفَأمِنَ"; hence the plural "were given fatḥa".]
His saying: ﴿وَهم يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ (while they are playing): it is said to anyone who is engaged in something that is of no benefit, or in error: "You are only playing (لاعِبٌ)". It was said of them: "ضُحًى وهم يَلْعَبُونَ" (in the forenoon while they are playing), meaning: while they are engaged in what is of no benefit to them.

zajjaj:99-99.t:
His saying: ﴿أفَأمِنُوا مَكْرَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: and did they feel secure from the punishment of Allah, that it might come upon them suddenly while they did not perceive?!
His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الأرْضَ مِن بَعْدِ أهْلِها أنْ لَوْ نَشاءُ أصَبْناهم بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 100] is also read "نَهْدِ", with nūn. Whoever reads "نَهْدِ" with nūn, its meaning is "أوَلَمْ نُبَيِّنْ" (have We not made clear), because your saying "هَدَيْتُهُ الطَّرِيقَ" means "بَيَّنْتُ لَهُ الطَّرِيقَ" (I made the way clear to him). Whoever reads it with yāʾ, the meaning is: "Has Allah not made clear to them that, if He willed, He would strike them for their sins?"
His saying: ﴿وَنَطْبَعُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 100] is not carried on (conjoined to) "أصَبْناهم"; the meaning is: "and We seal their hearts", because if it were carried on "أصَبْناهم", it would have been "وَلَطَبَعْنا", since that is past in form and in meaning. It is also permissible for it to be carried on the past, with its form being the form of the imperfect (future), just as "لَوْ نَشاءَ" means "لَوْ شِئْنا" (if We had willed).

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying: ﴿فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا مِن قَبْلُ كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الكافِرِينَ﴾: this is information about a people who will not believe, just as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36], and just as He said to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها الكافِرُونَ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 1] ﴿لا أعْبُدُ ما تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 2] ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 3]. This is information from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that these people will not believe.
Some people said: "فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا مِن قَبْلُ" means: they are not believers because of their denial. This is nothing (worthless), because His saying ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الكافِرِينَ﴾ indicates that their hearts had already been sealed. The position of the kāf in "كَذَلِكَ" is accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "In the like of that manner Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers".

zajjaj:102-102.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ وجَدْنا أكْثَرَهم لَفاسِقِينَ﴾: this "إنْ" comes, together with the lām, with the sense of tawkīd (emphasis) and oath, and it enters upon predicative statements; you say: "إنْ ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا لَقائِمًا" (I did indeed think Zayd was standing).
His saying: ﴿فَظَلَمُوا بِها﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 103] means: with regard to the signs that came to them; because when the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, they committed the most manifest wrong, since wrong (ẓulm) is putting a thing in other than its place: in place of the obligation to believe in them they put disbelief. That is the meaning of His saying: "فَظَلَمُوا بِها".

zajjaj:105-105.t: His saying: ﴿حَقِيقٌ عَلى أنْ لا أقُولَ عَلى اللَّهِ إلا الحَقَّ﴾ is also read: "حَقِيقٌ عَلَيَّ ألّا أقُولَ". Whoever reads "حَقِيقٌ عَلَيَّ ألّا أقُولَ", the meaning is: it is obligatory upon me to refrain from saying anything about Allah except the truth.

zajjaj:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ إنْ كُنْتَ جِئْتَ بِآيَةٍ فَأْتِ بِها إنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ﴾: Pharaoh asserted that it was not a sign as he claimed, for he had conceded his truthfulness if he brought a sign which created beings are incapable of producing.

zajjaj:107-107.t:
His saying: ﴿فَألْقى عَصاهُ﴾: if you wish, you may say "عَصاهُو" with the wāw, but the better usage is to drop it, I mean the wāw, because it is vowelless and the alif is vowelless, and the hāʾ is not a barrier.
His saying: ﴿فَإذا هي ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: Abū ʿUbayda and others said: "اَلثُّعْبانُ" is the serpent; someone else said: the male serpent. Allah said in another place: ﴿فَإذا هي حَيَّةٌ تَسْعى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 20]. And the meaning of "مُبِينٌ" is: clearly showing that it is a serpent.

zajjaj:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَـزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإذا هي بَيْضاءُ لِلنّاظِرِينَ﴾: the meaning of "نَزَعَ يَدَهُ" is: he brought it out and displayed it. He said in another place: ﴿وَأدْخِلْ يَدَكَ في جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ﴾ [al-Naml: 12], and in another place: ﴿واضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إلى جَناحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 22]. This is evidence that the meaning of drawing out his hand is bringing it out from the opening of his garment, and bringing it out from his side (جَناح). "جَناحُ الرَّجُلِ" is his upper arm; it has also been said: "جَناحُ الرَّجُلِ" is his flank. The interpretation of the two "wings" of a human being is that they are like the two wings of a bird, and they are the two upper arms.
His saying: ﴿تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 22] means: it comes out with its colour a pure, brilliant white; and Moses, according to what is reported, was dark-skinned (آدَم). ﴿مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 22] means: it comes out white with a whiteness that is not leprosy, a whiteness indicating that it is a sign. And the staff of Moses would only become a serpent when he displayed the sign with it, and then it would return to being a staff, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَنُعِيدُها سِيرَتَها الأُولى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 21].

zajjaj:109-109.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ لِلْمَلإ حَوْلَهُ إنَّ هَذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 34], and in this place: ﴿قالَ المَلأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾. "اَلْمَلَأُ" are the notables and the men of judgement; they were only called "مَلَأ" because they are filled (مُلِئُوا) with what is needed from them. It has also been read: "لَسَحّارٌ عَلِيمٌ" (a most skilful sorcerer).

zajjaj:110-110.t:
﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يُخْرِجَكم مِن أرْضِكُمْ﴾: Pharaoh said, answering them: ﴿فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾ (so what do you command?). It is also possible that "فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ" is from the speech of the notables, as though they were addressing Pharaoh and those close to him; and it is permissible that the address is to Pharaoh alone, because one says to an obeyed chief: "What do you (plural) think about this?", meaning: "What do you and your troops think?".
As for "ماذا": "ماذا" may properly be a single noun, in the position of the accusative (naṣb), the meaning being: "What thing do you command?"; and "ذا" may properly be in the place of "اَلَّذِي" (relative noun), with "ما" in the sense of the nominative (rafʿ), the meaning being: "What is it that you command?".

zajjaj:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿قالُوا أرْجِهْ وأخاهُ﴾: the explanation of "أرْجِهْ" is: postpone him; its meaning is: "Postpone his affair and do not hasten to a judgement in his matter, lest your haste become an argument against you".
In His saying "أرْجِهْ" there are three ways, all of which have been read: Abū ʿAmr read "أرْجِئْهُ وأخاهُ"; a group of the readers read "أرْجِهِ وأخاهُ"; and some of them read "أرْجِهْ وأخاهُ", with the hāʾ vowelless (sukūn). There are also ways in it which I do not know to have been read: it is permissible to say "أرْجِهُو وأخاهُ", "أرْجِهِي", "أرْجِئْهِي" and "أرْجِهُو", without hamza.
As for whoever read "أرْجِهْ" with the hāʾ vowelless, those skilled in grammar do not recognise it; they claim that the hāʾ of the pronoun is a noun which may not be made vowelless. One of the grammarians claimed that making it vowelless is permissible, and it has indeed, by my life, been transmitted in the readings, except that giving it a vowel is more common and better. This same person also claimed that the hāʾ of the feminine may be made vowelless, and this is not permissible. He cited as evidence for this a poem of unknown origin; he said: someone recited to me:
؎لَمّا رَأى أنْ لا دَعَهْ ولا شَبَعْ ∗∗∗ مالَ إلى أرْطاةِ حِقْفٍ فاضْطَجَعْ
(When he saw that there was neither ease nor fill, he turned to an arṭā shrub on a curving sand-dune and lay down.)
This is a poem whose author is unknown, and it is worth nothing; and even if a known poet had said it, it would be said to him: you have erred, for a poet may err.
He also recited another, more ignorant than this, namely his saying:
؎لَسْتُ إذَنْ لَزَغْبَلَهْ ∗∗∗ إنْ لَمْ أُغَيِّرْ بَكْلَتِي
؎إنْ لَمْ أُساوَ بِالطُوَلْ
(Then I am not [a son] of Zaghbala if I do not change my manner, if I am not made equal to the tall ones.)
So he made the hāʾ in "زَغْبَلَهْ" jussive (vowelless) and made it a hāʾ, whereas it is a tāʾ in continuous speech. This is a doctrine not worth stopping at.

zajjaj:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ ساحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾, and "سَحّارٍ": both have been read.
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّكم لَمِنَ المُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 114] means: along with the reward, you will have a lofty rank with me.

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿واسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ﴾ means: they sought to arouse their fear, until the people feared them.

zajjaj:117-117.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإذا هي تَلْقَفُ ما يَأْفِكُونَ﴾, and "تَلَقَّفُ", with the light and the doubled form. One says: "لَقَفْتُ الشَّيْءَ، ألْقَفُهُ" (I snatched the thing, I snatch it). The meaning of His saying "يَأْفِكُونَ" is: they bring forth falsehood (الإفْك), which is lying; that is because they claimed that their ropes and staffs were serpents, and they lied in that. It has been said that they used quicksilver and shaped them in the forms of serpents, and the quicksilver quivered because it does not stay still.
His saying: ﴿يُخَيَّلُ إلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أنَّها تَسْعى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 66]: then when Moses cast down his staff, it swallowed their staffs and their ropes. The poet said:
؎أنْتَ عَصا مُوسى الَّتِي لَمْ تَزَلْ ∗∗∗ تَلَقَّفُ ما يَأْفِكُهُ السّاحِرُ
(You are the staff of Moses, which never ceases to swallow up what the sorcerer falsely contrives.)
This verse was recited to Abū ʿUbayda, and al-Tawwazī, the companion of Abū ʿUbayda, claimed that he did not know it; yet it is sound in meaning.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنّاكم في الأرْضِ وجَعَلْنا لَكم فِيها مَعايِشَ﴾. The meaning of establishing (التَّمْكِين) in the land is granting possession and power. The meaning of "المَعايِش" may be that by which they live, and it may be the means of reaching that by which they live. Most of the readers read "مَعايِشَ" without hamza, but they have related it from Nāfiʿ with hamza. All the Basran grammarians claim that reading it with hamza is an error, and they mention that hamza occurs in this yāʾ only when it is an augment, as in "صَحِيفَةٌ" and "صَحائِفُ"; whereas "مَعايِشُ" is from "اَلْعَيْشُ", the yāʾ being radical. "صَحِيفَةٌ" is from "اَلصُّحُفِ", the yāʾ being an augment; it was given hamza only because it has no share in vowelling, and it has come near the end of the word and a vowel has become necessary for it, so they made hamza obligatory in it. And when you form the plural of "مَقامًا", you say "مَقاوِمُ", and the grammarians recited:
؎وَإنِّي لَقَوّامٌ مَقاوِمَ لَمْ يَكُنْ ∗∗∗ جَرِيرٌ ولا مَوْلى جَرِيرٍ يَقُومُها
(And I am one who stands much in stations (مَقاوِم) which neither Jarīr nor Jarīr's client would stand in.)
The grammarians are agreed in relating "مَصائِبُ" with hamza as the plural of "مُصِيبَةٌ", and they are agreed that the preferred form is "مَصاوِبُ"; and this, in their view, is anomalous (shādhdh) — I mean "مَصايِبُ". [Translator's note: the text here reads «مَصايِبُ» with yāʾ, although the form under discussion is «مَصائِبُ» with hamza.] In my view this is only a substitution [of hamza] for the wāw with kasra, just as they said "إسادَةٌ" for "وِسادَةٌ"; except that this substitution in the case of [the wāw] with kasra occurs at the beginning [of a word], as it does in that with ḍamma, as in "أُقِّتَتْ", which is only from "اَلْوَقْتُ"; while that with ḍamma is substituted in a non-initial position, as in "أدْوُرٌ", for which they say "أدْؤُرٌ"; so they treated the one with kasra on that pattern.
I know of no one who has explained this other than myself, and it is better than declaring something an error when the Arabs have uttered it and it has some ground in analogy; except that it is of the kind of substitution in which only what is heard [from the Arabs] is followed, and it is not made into a general analogical rule. As for what Nāfiʿ related, "مَعائِشَ" with hamza, I know no justification for it, except that the pronunciation of this yāʾ, which belongs to the root of the word, is vowelless in "مَعِيشَةٌ", so it took the form of "صَحِيفَةٌ", and he treated the plural accordingly. I do not like reading with hamza, since most people read without hamza. Even if it were something that takes hamza, both pronouncing the hamza fully and dropping it would be permissible; so how much more so when it is something with no basis for hamza at all — and this is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in which one ought to go by what the majority hold, because reading is an established practice (sunna), and so following [the transmitted reading] is what is most fitting in it, and following the majority is most fitting. Al-Akhfash claimed that in "مَصائِبَ" the hamza occurred only as a substitute for the wāw that was weakened in "مُصِيبَةٌ"; this is poor, [for] I am not obliged to say "مَقائِمُ" for "مَقامٌ", nor "مَعائِنُ" for "مَعُونَةٌ".

zajjaj:11-11.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْناكم ثُمَّ صَوَّرْناكم ثُمَّ قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لآدَمَ﴾. Al-Akhfash claimed that "ثُمَّ" here is in the sense of the wāw; this is an error, which neither al-Khalīl nor Sībawayh nor anyone whose Arabic is trusted allows. "ثُمَّ" is only for something that comes after what was mentioned before it, nothing else. The sense of this address is the mention, first, of the beginning of the creation of Adam; the meaning is only: "We began the creation of Adam, then We shaped him". The beginning of Adam's creation was dust; the proof of that is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرابٍ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 59]. So Allah began the creation of Adam as dust, and began the creation of Eve from one of his ribs; then the form came after that. This is the meaning of "خَلَقْناكم ثُمَّ صَوَّرْناكم", i.e. this is the origin of your creation; then Allah created drops of sperm, then they were shaped. So "ثُمَّ" is only for what comes after.
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿ثُمَّ قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لآدَمَ﴾, i.e. after the creation of Adam was completed, the angels were commanded to prostrate.
And His saying: ﴿إلا إبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السّاجِدِينَ﴾ is an exception not from the first [category], but he was among those commanded to prostrate; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿ما مَنَعَكَ ألا تَسْجُدَ إذْ أمَرْتُكَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 12]. By His saying ﴿إذْ أمَرْتُكَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 12] He showed that Iblīs was commanded to prostrate along with the angels. The meaning of ﴿ما مَنَعَكَ ألا تَسْجُدَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 12] involves treating "لا" as void; it is emphatic, the meaning being: "What prevented you from prostrating (ما مَنَعَكَ أنْ تَسْجُدَ)?" His asking him about this — while Allah already knew what had prevented him — is a rebuke to him, and to make plain that he was obstinate and had committed disobedience in opposition to Allah. Everyone who opposes Allah in His command and does not regard it as obligatory upon himself is an unbeliever by consensus: if someone abandoned a prayer saying "it is not obligatory", he would be an unbeliever by the consensus of the community. So Allah — exalted be His praise — made known that the disobedience of Iblīs was a disobedience of obstinacy and unbelief, and Allah has made known that he is one of the unbelievers, saying: ﴿إلا إبْلِيسَ أبى واسْتَكْبَرَ وكانَ مِنَ الكافِرِينَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 34]. The difference between the disobedience of Iblīs and the disobedience of Adam and Eve is that Iblīs was obstinate, persisted and did not repent, whereas Adam and Eve acknowledged the sin and said: ﴿رَبَّنا ظَلَمْنا أنْفُسَنا وإنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنا وتَرْحَمْنا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الخاسِرِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 23].

zajjaj:12-12.t:
Like "ألّا" in His saying ﴿ألا تَسْجُدَ﴾ is His saying: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29], i.e. "لِأنْ يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ (so that the People of the Book may know)", and the poet's saying:
؎أبى جُودُهُ ”لا“ البُخْلَ واسْتَعْجَلَتْ بِهِ ∗∗∗ ”نَعَمْ“ مِن فَتًى لا يَمْنَعُ الجُودَ قاتِلَهْ
(His generosity refused the "no" of avarice, and a "yes" hastened forth from a young man whom generosity — though it be his killer — does not hold back.)
They said: its meaning is "His generosity refused avarice (أبى جُودُهُ البُخْلَ)". Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: the transmitted wording is "أبى جُودَهُ البُخْلَ واسْتَعْجَلَتْ بِهِ نَعَمْ". What Abū ʿAmr said is good. The meaning is: "His generosity refused the 'لا' that makes a person miserly" — as though, when it is said "Do not be extravagant, and do not squander your wealth", his generosity refused this "لا", and a "نَعَمْ" hastened forth from him, and he said: "Yes, I will do it, and I will not abandon generosity". These two views on the verse are the views of the scholars. I see another interpretation of it which I consider good: I hold that "لا" is not void, and that "اَلْبُخْلَ" is accusative as a badal (substitute) for "لا", the meaning being: "His generosity refused avarice, and a 'yes' hastened forth from him".
The position of "ما" in His saying ﴿ما مَنَعَكَ ألا تَسْجُدَ﴾ is nominative; the meaning is: "What thing prevented you in [the matter of] prostration?" He did not say "such-and-such prevented me", but brought something that has the sense of an answer, while its wording is not that of an answer, because his saying ﴿أنا خَيْرٌ مِنهُ﴾ has the sense of "My superiority over him prevented me from prostrating". Like this in answering is when a man says "How were you?" and the other says "I am well", whereas the answer is "I was well"; but the sense is that he has answered him with what he needed, and added to it that he is well at the time of being asked. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فاخْرُجْ إنَّكَ مِنَ الصّاغِرِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 13], and Allah informed him that he was abased by this act.

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قالَ أنْظِرْنِي إلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾, i.e. defer me until the Day of Resurrection. His request for respite until the Day of Resurrection itself was not granted; he was told that he was respited until the day of the known time.

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿قالَ فَبِما أغْوَيْتَنِي لأقْعُدَنَّ لَهم صِراطَكَ المُسْتَقِيمَ﴾. On His saying "أغْوَيْتَنِي" there are two views. Some said: "because You have led me astray (فَبِما أضْلَلْتَنِي)"; and some said: "because You called me to something through which I went astray", i.e. "I went astray because of Adam". ﴿لأقْعُدَنَّ لَهم صِراطَكَ المُسْتَقِيمَ﴾: there is no disagreement among the grammarians that "عَلى" is omitted; of this kind is your saying "ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ الظَّهْرَ، والبَطْنَ (Zayd was struck on the back and the belly)".

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهم مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ ومِن خَلْفِهِمْ وعَنْ أيْمانِهِمْ وعَنْ شَمائِلِهِمْ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Then I shall come at them in [leading them into] error from all their sides". It was said: "مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ" means "I shall lead them astray in everything that is anticipated"; and it was also said: "I shall make them fear poverty". The reality — and Allah knows best — is: "I shall turn myself to them in leading them astray from all their sides".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالَ اخْرُجْ مِنها مَذْءُومًا مَدْحُورًا﴾. The meaning of "مَذْؤُومٌ" is like the meaning of "مَذْمُومٌ (blamed)". One says "ذَأمْتُهُ، أذْأمُهُ، ذَأْمًا" when you have terrified him and blamed him. [Translator's note: the text reads «رَعَبْتَهُ» (terrified him); the lexicons usually gloss ذَأم as «عِبْتَهُ» (found fault with him).] The meaning of "مَدْحُورًا" is: banished far from the mercy of Allah.
And His saying: ﴿لَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنهُمْ﴾: this lām is the lām of the oath, entering as a preparation for the matter, "لَأمْلَأنَّ". The speech has the sense of condition and consequence, as though it were said: "Whoever follows you, I will punish him", and the lām entered for intensification and emphasis. The lām of "لَأمْلَأنَّ" is the lām of the oath, and the lām of "مَن تَبِعَكَ" is a preparation (tawṭiʾa) for it. In speech, "واللَّهِ مَن جاءَكَ لَأضْرِبَنَّهُ (By Allah, whoever comes to you, I will surely strike him)" is permissible, but "واللَّهِ لَمَن جاءَكَ أضْرِبُهُ" is not permissible when you mean "لَأضْرِبَنَّهُ"; but "واللَّهِ لَمَن جاءَكَ أضْرِبْهُ" is permissible, meaning "لَأضْرِبَنَّهُ". Some said — concerning His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهم مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ ومِن خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 17] —: i.e. I shall lead them astray in what they were commanded to do.
And His saying: ﴿وَعَنْ شَمائِلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 17], i.e. I shall lead them astray in what they were forbidden. What I think — and Allah knows best — on this view is: "I shall lead them astray until they deny the matters of the bygone nations, [and deny] the Resurrection", as was mentioned regarding this. And the meaning of ﴿وَعَنْ أيْمانِهِمْ وعَنْ شَمائِلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 17] is: I shall lead them astray in what they understand; because of earning it is said "That is for what your two hands have earned", even if the hands committed nothing; rather, of everything a doer does it is said "your two hands have earned", because the hands are the principal [instrument] of action, so they were made a figure for everything done with other than them. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 10], and said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيكُمْ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 182], and said: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ وتَبَّ﴾ [al-Masad: 1], then explained, saying: ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْهُ مالُهُ وما كَسَبَ﴾ [al-Masad: 2].

zajjaj:126-126.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما تَنْقِمُ مِنّا﴾ (and you resent nothing in us): one says "نَقِمْتُ، أنْقِمُ" and "نَقِمْتُ، أنْقَمُ"; the better is "نَقَمْتُ أنْقِمُ". The reading is "وَما تَنْقِمُ", and it is the more eloquent of the two dialects.
[Translator's note: the first form is vowelled in the text as "نَقِمْتُ، أنْقِمُ"; it is translated as written.]
His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا أفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْرًا﴾ means: let it envelop us.

zajjaj:127-127.t:
His saying: ﴿أتَذَرُ مُوسى وقَوْمَهُ لِيُفْسِدُوا في الأرْضِ ويَذَرَكَ وآلِهَتَكَ﴾ is also read "وَإلاهَتَكَ" (and your worship), and "وَيَذَرُكَ وآلِهَتَكَ" (with the nominative) is permissible. Whoever puts "وَيَذَرَكَ" in the accusative makes it refer back, by means of the wāw, to the answer of the interrogative; the meaning is: "Will it come from you that you leave Moses, and that he leaves you?". Whoever says "وَيَذَرُكَ" makes it resumptive (mustaʾnaf); the meaning will be: "Will you leave Moses while he leaves you and your gods?". The better is that it be conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "أتَذَرُ", so that it is: "Will you leave Moses, and will Moses leave you?", that is: "Will you allow him this?".
As for whoever reads "وَآلِهَتَكَ", the meaning is that Pharaoh had idols which his people worshipped as a means of drawing near to him.

zajjaj:129-129.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُهْلِكَ عَدُوَّكُمْ﴾: "عَسى" expresses hope and apprehension, except that whatever Allah makes a matter of hope is certain; and that is the meaning of the exegetes' saying: "عَسى" from Allah is certain.
The meaning of ﴿فَيَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ is: He sees that as something actually occurring from you; because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, does not requite them for the sins He knows of them, which He knows they will inevitably commit; He requites them only for what has actually occurred from them.

zajjaj:130-130.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أخَذْنا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِالسِّنِينَ﴾: "اَلسِّنِينَ" in the speech of the Arabs means droughts. One says: "the year (السَّنَة) touched them", meaning the drought of the year, the hardship of the year, and the shortage of fruits.
﴿لَعَلَّهم يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾: they were seized with adversity only because states of hardship soften hearts and make one desire what is with Allah and desire returning to Him. Do you not see His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإذا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ في البَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إلا إيّاهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 67]? And He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإذا أنْعَمْنا عَلى الإنْسانِ أعْرَضَ ونَأى بِجانِبِهِ وإذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 51].

zajjaj:131-131.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا جاءَتْهُمُ الحَسَنَةُ قالُوا لَنا هَذِهِ﴾ means: when abundance came to them, they said: we have been given this because we deserve it. ﴿وَإنْ تُصِبْهم سَيِّئَةٌ﴾ means: drought or harm, ﴿يَطَّيَّرُوا بِمُوسى ومَن مَعَهُ﴾: the meaning (underlying form) is "يَتَطَيَّرُوا"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because they are from the same place of articulation, the tip of the tongue and the roots of the front teeth. The explanation of His saying ﴿يَطَّيَّرُوا﴾ is: they regard as an ill omen. The Arabs said "اَلطِّيرَةُ" and "يَتَطَيَّرُ" only of what they dislike, according to what they had agreed upon among themselves; they made that a matter from which they drew ill omens. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ألا إنَّما طائِرُهم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾; the meaning is: "Indeed, the ill omen that overtakes them is only what they have been promised in the Hereafter, not what befalls them in this world". Some said: "طائِرُهم" means their lot; and the meaning is the same.

zajjaj:132-132.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقالُوا مَهْما تَأْتِنا بِهِ مِن آيَةٍ لِتَسْحَرَنا بِها﴾: some grammarians claimed that the origin of "مَهْما" is "ما ما تَأْتِنا بِهِ", but the hāʾ was substituted for the first alif so that the wording would differ. So the first "ما" is the "ما" of the conditional (jazāʾ), and the second "ما" is the one that is added to emphasise the conditional. The grammarians' evidence for that is that there is none of the conditional particles to which "ما" is not added. Allah, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿فَإمّا تَثْقَفَنَّهم في الحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَن خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 57], like your saying: "If you come upon them in war, scatter them"; and likewise His saying: ﴿وَإمّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 28]; and this is frequent in the Book of Allah.
They also said: it is permissible that "مَهْ" be in the sense of restraining, as you say "مَهْ", meaning: hold back; and the second "ما" is for the condition and its apodosis, as though they said, and Allah knows best: "Hold back! Whatever sign you bring us…".
The first explanation is the (correct) speech, and people's usage follows it. And there is nothing of consequence in the explanation in this (second view), because the difference between these two explanations disrupts the meaning of the speech.
[Translator's note: the text reads «أنَّ أصْلَ "مَهْما": "ما تَأْتِنا بِهِ"», i.e. the second "ما" appears to have dropped out of the quoted origin; the following sentences speak of a first and a second "ما", so it is rendered "ما ما". The final sentence is obscure in the Arabic and is translated literally.]

zajjaj:133-133.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الطُّوفانَ﴾: al-Akhfash said: "اَلطُّوفانُ" is the plural of "طُوفانَةٌ". It was said in the exegesis that al-ṭūfān is the rain that drowns by its abundance; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said in the story of Noah: ﴿فَأخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وهم ظالِمُونَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 14]. It has also been said: "اَلطُّوفانُ" is a great death (plague).
His saying: ﴿والقُمَّلَ﴾: Abū ʿUbayda said of it: it is al-ḥanmān, the small ticks. Its explanation is disputed: some said they are creatures smaller than lice.
﴿والدَّمَ﴾: it was said that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, turned their water into blood, so that the Israelite would draw water sweet and clear, and when the Copt took it, it turned into clear blood.
His saying: ﴿آياتٍ مُفَصَّلاتٍ﴾ means: some of them were separate from others; it is said that between one sign and the next there were eight days. And frogs were sent upon them, entering their clothes and their food. "آياتٍ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and they are the signs (tokens).

zajjaj:134-134.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا وقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّجْزُ﴾: "اَلرِّجْزُ" is a name for punishment. ﴿قالُوا يا مُوسى ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ بِما عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ لَئِنْ كَشَفْتَ عَنّا الرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ ولَنُرْسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾. They had subjected the Children of Israel to severe toil, until they said to Moses: ﴿أُوذِينا مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَأْتِيَنا ومِن بَعْدِ ما جِئْتَنا﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 129]. It is said that they used to employ the Children of Israel in moulding bricks; Pharaoh and his companions among the Copts used to do that to the Children of Israel, and when Moses was sent, they gave them the bricks to mould but withheld the straw from them, so that this would be harder on them.

zajjaj:136-136.t:
His saying: ﴿فانْتَقَمْنا مِنهم فَأغْرَقْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾: al-yamm is the sea, and so it is in the earlier scriptures.
﴿وَكانُوا عَنْها غافِلِينَ﴾ means: they did not take heed of the signs that came down upon them.

zajjaj:137-137.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأوْرَثْنا القَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشارِقَ الأرْضِ ومَغارِبَها﴾ means the Children of Israel; among them were David and Solomon, who ruled the land.
His saying: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الحُسْنى﴾ means: what Allah promised them of destroying their enemy and making them successors in the land. ﴿وَدَمَّرْنا ما كانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وقَوْمُهُ وما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ﴾, and "يَعْرُشُونَ": both (are read). One says: "عَرَشَ، يَعْرِشُ، ويَعْرُشُ" when he builds.

zajjaj:138-138.t: The meaning of ﴿يَعْكُفُونَ عَلى أصْنامٍ لَهُمْ﴾ is: they persevere in (devotion to) them and cling to them. It is said of everyone who clings to a thing and perseveres in it: "عَكَفَ، يَعْكِفُ، ويَعْكُفُ"; and from this, the one who keeps to the mosque is called "مُعْتَكِفٌ".

zajjaj:139-139.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ مُتَبَّرٌ ما هم فِيهِ وباطِلٌ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾: "مُتَبَّرٌ" means destroyed and ruined. Every broken vessel is called "مُتَبَّرٌ", and its fragments are called "التِّبْرُ".

zajjaj:140-140.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ أغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أبْغِيكم إلَهًا﴾ means: shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, ﴿وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكم عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾ (when He has favoured you above the worlds)?

zajjaj:141-141.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذْ أنْجَيْناكم مِن آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾: the meaning is: "And remember when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh", ﴿يَسُومُونَكم سُوءَ العَذابِ﴾: the meaning of "يَسُومُونَكم" is: they inflict upon you.

zajjaj:142-142.t:
His saying: ﴿وَواعَدْنا مُوسى﴾, and "وَوَعَدْنا مُوسى" (also read), ﴿ثَلاثِينَ لَيْلَةً وأتْمَمْناها بِعَشْرٍ﴾: it was said that Allah commanded him to fast thirty days and to do during them what would bring him near to Allah; and it was said that during the ten the Torah was sent down to him and he was spoken to in them. Some said: when he had fasted thirty days, he disliked the changed odour of his mouth, so he cleaned his teeth with a stick of carob; the angels said: "We used to smell from your mouth the scent of musk, and you have spoiled it with the tooth-stick", so ten nights were added for him. And He said in another place: ﴿وَإذْ واعَدْنا مُوسى أرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 51]; this is evidence that the appointment was forty complete nights; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.
His saying: ﴿وَقالَ مُوسى لأخِيهِ هارُونَ اخْلُفْنِي في قَوْمِي﴾: "هارُونَ" with fatḥa is permissible, and it is in the position of the genitive (jarr) as a badal (substitute) for "أخِيهِ"; and "لِأخِيهِ هارُونُ", with ḍamma on the nūn, is permissible, the meaning being: "And Moses said to his brother: O Aaron, take my place among my people".

zajjaj:143-143.t:
﴿وَلَمّا جاءَ مُوسى لِمِيقاتِنا﴾ means: at the time We appointed for him. ﴿وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾: Allah spoke to Moses directly; Allah distinguished him in that there was no one between him and Allah, exalted be His praise, in what he heard, nor an angel through whom Allah made him hear His speech. When he heard the speech, he said: ﴿رَبِّ أرِنِي أنْظُرْ إلَيْكَ﴾, that is: You have addressed me from where I do not see You; the meaning is: show me Yourself.
His saying: ﴿أرِنِي أنْظُرْ﴾: (أنْظُرْ) is jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the imperative. ﴿قالَ لَنْ تَرانِي﴾: and lan is negation of what is in the future. ﴿وَلَكِنِ انْظُرْ إلى الجَبَلِ فَإنِ اسْتَقَرَّ مَكانَهُ فَسَوْفَ تَرانِي فَلَمّا تَجَلّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ﴾ means: appeared and became manifest. ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا﴾: "دَكًّا" with tanwīn is permissible, and "دَكاءَ" without tanwīn, that is: He made it pounded flat with the ground. One says: "دَكَكْتُ الشَّيْءَ أدُكُّهُ دَكًّا" when I pound it flat; and "اَلدَّكّاءُ" and "اَلدَّكّاواتُ" are the hillocks that are level with the ground, rising from it, not reaching the size of a mountain.
His saying: ﴿وَخَرَّ مُوسى صَعِقًا﴾: "صَعِقًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It was said that he fell down dead, and it was said that he fell down unconscious. ﴿فَلَمّا أفاقَ﴾: one hardly says of a dead man "he has recovered (أفاقَ) from his death", but rather of one who has fainted, and of one whose mind has gone, "he has recovered from his ailment"; for Allah, exalted be His praise, said concerning those who died: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْناكم مِن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 56].
His saying: ﴿قالَ سُبْحانَكَ﴾ means: declaring You free of every evil. It has come from the Prophet ﷺ that saying "سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ" is declaring Allah free of evil; and the lexicographers say the same, without knowing what is reported on it from the Prophet ﷺ; but they agree unanimously on its explanation.
His saying: ﴿وَأنا أوَّلُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ means: the first of those who believe that You are not seen in this world. This is the meaning of ﴿أرِنِي أنْظُرْ إلَيْكَ﴾ to the end of the verse, and it is the view of the people of knowledge and the people of the Sunna.
Some people said: the meaning of "أرِنِي أنْظُرْ إلَيْكَ" is: show me a mighty matter whose like is not seen in this world, of what the constitution of Moses could not bear. They said: so He informed him that he would not see that matter, and that the meaning of ﴿فَلَمّا تَجَلّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ﴾ is: the command of his Lord became manifest. This is a mistake which the lexicographers do not recognise, nor is there in the speech any evidence that Moses wanted to see a mighty matter among the matters of Allah. Allah had already shown him signs in his own person beyond which there is no limit: He had shown him his staff as a manifest serpent, and shown him his hand coming out white without blemish, while he was dark-skinned, and He parted the sea with his staff. So He had shown him great signs sufficient to make it unnecessary for him to ask for some mighty matter among the matters of Allah. Rather, when he heard the speech of Allah, he said: "My Lord, show me (Yourself) that I may look at You; I have heard Your speech, and I love to see You". So Allah, exalted be His praise, informed him that he would not see Him.

zajjaj:144-144.t:
Then Allah commanded him to thank Him, and said: ﴿يا مُوسى إنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلى النّاسِ﴾, that is: I have taken you as chosen above people, ﴿بِرِسالاتِي وبِكَلامِي﴾ (by My messages and by My speech). Had he only followed the speech of other than Allah, He would not have said "by My messages and by My speech", because the angels descend to the prophets with the speech of Allah.
[Translator's note: "تَبِعَ" (followed) is as in the text; the sense of the argument suggests "heard" (سَمِعَ).]
His saying: ﴿فَخُذْ ما آتَيْتُكَ وكُنْ مِنَ الشّاكِرِينَ﴾ (so take what I have given you and be among the grateful).

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَيا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أنْتَ وزَوْجُكَ الجَنَّةَ﴾: this is the preferred usage — I mean the mention of "أنْتَ". You say "اِذْهَبْ أنْتَ وزَيْدٌ (Go, you and Zayd)"; if you said "اِذْهَبْ وزَيْدٌ", it would be ugly. We have explained this previously.
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبا هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ﴾: some said it was the ear of grain (wheat); and it was said it was the grapevine.
And His saying: ﴿فَتَكُونا مِنَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾: the best is that "فَتَكُونا" be in the position of the accusative, as the answer to the command with the fāʾ, i.e. "for if you two approach it, you will be among the wrongdoers". It may also be in the position of the jussive (majzūm), as conjoined to His saying: "وَلا تَقْرَبا فَتَكُونا", i.e. "and do not be among the wrongdoers (فَلا تَكُونا مِنَ الظّالِمِينَ)".

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُما الشَّيْطانُ﴾ indicates — and Allah knows best — the sense of His saying: ﴿وَقالَ ما نَهاكُما رَبُّكُما عَنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إلا أنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾. "مَلِكَيْنِ (two kings)" is also permissible, because His saying ﴿هَلْ أدُلُّكَ عَلى شَجَرَةِ الخُلْدِ ومُلْكٍ لا يَبْلى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 120] points to "مَلِكَيْنِ", and I reckon it has been read so. So it indicates — and Allah knows best — that the speech was only a whispering from Iblīs. But the better [view] is that it was an address, because of His saying: ﴿وَقاسَمَهُما إنِّي لَكُما لَمِنَ النّاصِحِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 21], i.e. he swore to them; ﴿فَدَلاهُما بِغُرُورٍ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 22], i.e. he lowered them into disobedience by deceiving them; ﴿فَلَمّا ذاقا الشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُما سَوْآتُهُما﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 22], i.e. their private parts became apparent to them. "السَّوْءَة" is only a metonym (kināya) for the private part, though the origin of the naming is "اَلسَّوْءَةُ (the shameful thing)".

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَطَفِقا يَخْصِفانِ عَلَيْهِما مِن ورَقِ الجَنَّةِ﴾. The meaning of "طَفِقا" is: they set about doing. The more common form is "طَفِقَ، يَطْفَقُ", and "طَفَقَ، يَطْفَقُ" has also been related, with kasra on the fāʾ. [Translator's note: as printed, the vowelling of the two forms does not match the description; the second form is presumably «طَفَقَ يَطْفِقُ», with kasra on the fāʾ of the imperfect.] It was said that those leaves of the Garden were fig leaves. The meaning of "يَخْصِفانِ" is: they were placing leaf upon leaf; from this the cobbler (الخَصّاف) who patches sandals is said to be one who "يَخْصِفُ". The poet said:
؎أوْ يَخْصِفُ النَّعْلَ لَهْفِي أيَّةً صَنَعا
(…or he stitches the sandal — alas for me, what a deed he did!)
"يَخْصِفانِ" and "يَخَصِّفانِ" are also permissible; the origin is kasra on the khāʾ, [or] its fatḥa, with doubling of the ṣād, and the meaning would then be "يَخْتَصِفانِ". In this verse there is proof that uncovering and exposing the private parts has been ugly ever since Adam. Do you not see that He mentioned the gravity of it in the disobedience, saying: ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُما الشَّيْطانُ لِيُبْدِيَ لَهُما ما وُورِيَ عَنْهُما مِن سَوْآتِهِما﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 20], and that the two of them hastened to cover themselves because of the ugliness of exposure?
And His saying: ﴿وُورِيَ عَنْهُما﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 20]: "أُورِيَ" is permissible in it, because the wāw has ḍamma, and if you wish you may substitute hamza for it; but the reading is followed in that, and the well-known reading and the script of the muṣḥaf are "وُورِيَ" with wāw. And the meaning of ﴿إلا أنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 20] … and His saying ﴿ذاقا الشَّجَرَةَ﴾ indicates that they merely tasted it and did not go far in eating. [Translator's note: the sentence about ﴿إلا أنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾ is left without a predicate in the text.]

zajjaj:26-26.t:
And His saying: ﴿يا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْكم لِباسًا يُوارِي سَوْآتِكم ورِيشًا﴾; it is also read "وَرِياشًا". "اَلرِّيشُ" is clothing; the Arabs say "أعْطَيْتُهُ بِرِيشَتِهِ", i.e. with his clothing. "اَلرِّيشُ" is everything that covers a man in his body and his livelihood; one says "تَرَيَّشَ فُلانٌ", i.e. he came to have that by which he lives. Sībawayh and others recited:
؎فَرِيشِي مِنكُمُ وهَوايَ مَعْكم ∗∗∗ وإنْ كانَتْ زِيارَتُكم لِماما
(My livelihood comes from you and my love is with you, even if your visits are but rare.)
﴿وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى﴾ with "اللِّباسُ" in the nominative. Whoever puts it in the accusative conjoins it to "الرِّيش", the meaning being "We have sent down upon you the garment of piety", and puts "خَيْرٌ" in the nominative by "ذَلِكَ". Whoever puts "اللِّباس" in the nominative does so in one of two ways. One is that it be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with "ذَلِكَ" being its description, and "خَيْرٌ" the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the meaning is: "And the garment of piety referred to is best". It may also be that "وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى" is nominative by implying "هو", the meaning being: "it is the garment of piety", i.e. "covering the private parts is the garment of the God-fearing"; then He said: ﴿ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾. And it may be that "لِباسُ التَّقْوى" is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and "ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ" [its predicate], "خَيْرٌ" being nominative by it as the khabar of "ذَلِكَ", with "ذَلِكَ" standing in the place of "هو", as though — and Allah knows best — it were: "And the garment of piety, it is best", because demonstratives come close to the pronoun in the referring back of the reference. The first two interpretations are clearer in Arabic.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ يَراكم هو وقَبِيلُهُ مِن حَيْثُ لا تَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾: "حَيْثُ" is in the position of the genitive, but it is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma. Its origin is to be pausal (vowelless), because it is not for a specific place, and what follows it is a ṣila (relative clause) to it, not something it is annexed to. Some of the Arabs say "وَمِن حَيْثَ خَرَجْتَ (and from where you went out)", with fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and some of them say "مِن حَوْثُ خَرَجْتَ". Do not read with these two dialect forms, because neither of them has been read, nor are they as good as "حَيْثُ" built on ḍamma.
And His saying: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا الشَّياطِينَ أوْلِياءَ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: "جَعَلْنا" in the language is of several kinds. Among them is "I placed (جَعَلْتُ) part of the thing above another part", i.e. I made it and arranged it in this form. Among them is "Zayd made (جَعَلَ) so-and-so intelligent", whose interpretation is: he called him "intelligent". And among them is "he began (جَعَلَ) saying such-and-such", whose interpretation is that he set about speaking. As for the meaning of the verse, it is of two kinds — and Allah knows best. One is that the unbelievers were punished by having the devils given power over them, increasing them in their error as a punishment for their unbelief, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنّا أرْسَلْنا الشَّياطِينَ عَلى الكافِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهم أزًّا﴾ [Maryam: 83], i.e. driving them to acts of disobedience with violent driving, thrusting them into the severity of error. And "إنّا جَعَلْنا الشَّياطِينَ أوْلِياءَ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ" may mean: We have made the devils and the unbelievers equal in going away from Allah, as He said: ﴿المُنافِقُونَ والمُنافِقاتُ بَعْضُهم مِن بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Tawba: 67].

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإذا فَعَلُوا فاحِشَةً﴾: the meaning of "اَلْفاحِشَةُ" is a sin whose ugliness is severe. ﴿قالُوا وجَدْنا عَلَيْها آباءَنا واللَّهُ أمَرَنا بِها﴾: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that He does not command indecency, because His wisdom and all that He has created show that He does only what is deemed good; so how could He command indecency? He has argued against them elsewhere with what we have explained in Sūrat al-Anʿām.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أمَرَ رَبِّي بِالقِسْطِ﴾, i.e. with justice. How could One who is known to do nothing but wisdom, and to establish nothing of His command but justice, command indecency? If He commands justice — and "اَلْعَدْلُ (justice)" is what stands in souls as being upright, which no discerning person denies — then how [could He command] indecency?! "اَلْفَحْشاءُ" is that whose ugliness is great. Then He rebuked them, saying: ﴿أتَقُولُونَ عَلى اللَّهِ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 28], i.e. do you lie against Him?
And His saying: ﴿وَأقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكم عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾, i.e. at the time of every prayer, direct yourselves to Him with your prayer.
﴿وادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾, i.e. making obedience sincerely His.
He argued against them in their denial of the Resurrection — and it is connected to His saying: ﴿فِيها تَحْيَوْنَ وفِيها تَمُوتُونَ ومِنها تُخْرَجُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 25] — saying: ﴿كَما بَدَأكم تَعُودُونَ﴾, i.e. your resurrection is not harder than your origination.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَرِيقًا هَدى وفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضَّلالَةُ﴾: its meaning is that He led a party astray, against whom error was due. Then He said: ﴿إنَّهُمُ اتَّخَذُوا الشَّياطِينَ أوْلِياءَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾; had it been read "أنَّهُمُ اتَّخَذُوا الشَّياطِينَ" [with fatḥa, "because they took"], it would be permissible, but there is consensus on the kasra.
And His saying: ﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ أنَّهم مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ shows that people who profess Islam and claim that whoever is an unbeliever without knowing that he is an unbeliever is not an unbeliever, are invalidating the matter of their own creed, because Allah — exalted be His praise — has informed us that they reckon they are rightly guided; and there is no disagreement among the people of language that "الحُسْبان (reckoning)" has no interpretation other than what is known of the meaning of "حَسِبَ". The proof that Allah has called them "unbelievers" because of their supposition is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما خَلَقْنا السَّماءَ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما باطِلا ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 27]; so He made known that by supposition they are unbelievers, and that they will be punished.
And His saying: ﴿يا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكم عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 31]: this is a command to cover oneself in the prayers. The people of the Jāhiliyya used to circumambulate naked, saying: "We will not circumambulate the House in clothes in which we have sinned." The woman too used to circumambulate naked, except that she would tie around her waist things made of cut leather thongs, which the Arabs call "اَلرَّهْطُ". A woman circumambulating wearing a rahṭ said:
؎اَلْيَوْمَ يَبْدُو بَعْضُهُ أوْ كُلُّهْ ∗∗∗ فَما بَدا مِنهُ فَلا أُحِلُّهْ
(Today some or all of it shows; and whatever of it shows, I do not make it lawful.)
She meant the private part, because the thongs do not cover completely. So after mentioning the punishment of Adam and Eve — that their private parts became apparent to them — Allah commanded covering at the time of every prayer, having first made known that nakedness and exposure of the private parts have been detested ever since Adam.

zajjaj:145-145.t:
Then Allah, exalted be His praise, made known that He had given him everything he needed in the matter of religion, along with the signs He had shown him, and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَكَتَبْنا لَهُ في الألْواحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وتَفْصِيلا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾. It was said in the exegesis that they were two tablets; and it is permissible in the language to call two tablets "ألْواحٌ" (tablets, plural), and it is possible that "ألْواحٌ" is the plural of more than two.
His saying: ﴿فَخُذْها بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ means: take it with strength in your religion and your argument.
His saying: ﴿وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُوا بِأحْسَنِها﴾: there are two aspects in this. It is similar to His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ القَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أحْسَنَهُ﴾ [al-Zumar: 18], and similar to His saying: ﴿واتَّبِعُوا أحْسَنَ ما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكم مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [al-Zumar: 55]. So it bears two aspects. One of them is that they were commanded to do good and forbidden evil, and were made to know what was due to them in that; so it was said: "And command your people to take the best of it". It is also possible that it is like what we have been commanded concerning retaliating after being wronged, and like retaliation (qiṣāṣ) for wounds, when He said: ﴿وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وغَفَرَ إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِن عَزْمِ الأُمُورِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 43], ﴿وَلَمَنِ انْتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ ما عَلَيْهِمْ مِن سَبِيلٍ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 41]. All of this is good, but pardon is better than retaliation, and patience is better than avenging oneself.

zajjaj:146-146.t:
His saying: ﴿سَأصْرِفُ عَنْ آياتِيَ الَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ في الأرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الحَقِّ﴾ means: I will make their recompense being led astray from the guidance of My signs. The meaning of "يَتَكَبَّرُونَ" is that they consider themselves the best of creation and that they have rights which others do not have. This attribute belongs to none but Allah, exalted be His praise, exclusively, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who has power and excellence the like of which is not [found]; and that deserves that He be called "اَلْمُتَكَبِّرُ" (the Supremely Great). No one has the right to be arrogant, because people are equal in rights, so no one has what another does not have; and Allah, exalted be His praise, is al-Mutakabbir. Allah made known that these people are arrogant in the land without right.
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لا يُؤْمِنُوا بِها وإنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ لا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلا وإنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلا﴾: "the way of al-ghayy" is the way of error. One says: "غَوى الرَّجُلُ، يَغْوِي، غَيًّا، وهو غاوٍ" when he goes astray.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾: "ذَلِكَ" may properly be nominative (rafʿ), that is: "their affair is that"; and it may be accusative (naṣb) in the sense of "Allah did that to them because they denied Our signs".
﴿وَكانُوا عَنْها غافِلِينَ﴾: "غافِلِينَ" may properly mean, and Allah knows best, that in their abandoning belief in them, reflection on them and pondering over them, they were in the position of the heedless; and it may be "and they were heedless of answering to them (عَنْ جَوابِها)", as you say: "How heedless so-and-so is of what is intended for him!".

zajjaj:148-148.t:
His saying: ﴿واتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسى مِن بَعْدِهِ مِن حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾, also "مِن حَلْيِهِمْ" and "مِن حِلِيِّهِمْ". Whoever reads "مِن حَلْيِهِمْ": "اَلْحَلْيُ" is a name for the gold and silver with which one adorns oneself. Whoever reads "مِن حُلِيِّهِمْ" with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, it is the plural of "حَلْيٌ" on the pattern "حُلِيٌّ", like "حَقْوٌ" and "حُقِيٌّ". Whoever gives the ḥāʾ a kasra and says "مِن حِلْيِهِمْ" makes the ḥāʾ follow the kasra of the lām.
The meaning of "مِن بَعْدِهِ" is: after he went to the appointment and Aaron took his place among his people. They had jewellery which they would gather in their days of festivity, and the Children of Israel had jewellery for the Tent (al-qubba). Then al-Sāmirī said to them (and he was a man obeyed among them, of standing), and they had asked Moses to make for them a god to worship, as they had seen the people of Pharaoh worshipping idols, so al-Sāmirī collected that jewellery; and that is their saying: ﴿وَلَكِنّا حُمِّلْنا أوْزارًا مِن زِينَةِ القَوْمِ فَقَذَفْناها﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 87], that is: we threw them, ﴿فَكَذَلِكَ ألْقى السّامِرِيُّ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 87], that is: and likewise al-Sāmirī threw down the jewellery that he had, and cast it into the calf. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿واتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسى مِن بَعْدِهِ مِن حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلا جَسَدًا﴾. "اَلْجَسَدُ" is that which does not reason or discern; the meaning of "اَلْجَسَدُ" is only that of "اَلْجُثَّةُ" (a body, a mere bulk).
﴿لَهُ خُوارٌ﴾ means: "it had a sound". It has also been said: "لَهُ خُؤارٌ", with khāʾ and with jīm, and both are sounds. He had made it as these devices are made that produce sounds by means of wind (?), and he put it in a house and informed them that their god and the god of Moses was with me. It is said in the exegesis that its sound was heard once only. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا أنَّهُ لا يُكَلِّمُهم ولا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلا﴾, that is: it does not show them a way to any proof.
[Translator's note: the text spells the variant "خُؤارٌ" with khāʾ although it says "with khāʾ and with jīm"; the jīm form intended is presumably "جُؤارٌ". The sentence "Then al-Sāmirī said to them…" is not completed in the text. "بِالخَيْلِ" (literally "with horses") is as in the text, probably a corruption of "بِالرِّيحِ" (by wind) or similar. "عِنْدِي" (with me) is as written, though the context suggests "with him"; "حِلْيِهِمْ" in the kasra sentence is as written.]

zajjaj:149-149.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا سُقِطَ في أيْدِيهِمْ﴾: it is said of a man who regrets what he has done and grieves over what he neglected: "قَدْ سُقِطَ في يَدِهِ، وأُسْقِطَ". "سُقِطَ" has been transmitted in the reading; the meaning is: "and when regret fell into their hands", just as you say of one who comes to have something, even if it is something that cannot be in the hand: "something disagreeable from this has come into his hand", likening what arises in the heart and the soul to what is seen with the eye.

zajjaj:150-150.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا رَجَعَ مُوسى إلى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبانَ أسِفًا﴾: "غَضْبانَ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is on the pattern "فَعْلانَ", and it has (a feminine) "فَعْلى", like "غَضْبى"; it is a diptote (not fully declined) because it contains the alif and nūn, like the two alifs of "حَمْراءَ". "اَلْأسِفُ" is one who is intensely angry; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلَمّا آسَفُونا انْتَقَمْنا مِنهُمْ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 55], that is: when they angered Us.
His saying: ﴿أعَجِلْتُمْ أمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾: one says "عَجِلْتُ الأمْرَ، والشَّيْءَ": I got ahead of it; and "أعْجَلْتُهُ": I urged it on.
﴿قالَ ابْنَ أُمَّ﴾ with fatḥa; and if you wish, "اِبْنَ أُمِّ" with kasra. As for whoever says "اِبْنَ أُمَّ" with fatḥa: they gave fatḥa in "اِبْنَ أُمَّ" and "اِبْنَ عَمَّ" only because of their frequent use of this noun, and because the vocative is speech that tolerates omission, so they made "اِبْنَ" and "أُمَّ" a single thing, like "خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ" (fifteen). Whoever says "اِبْنَ أُمِّ" with kasra annexes it to himself (the first person) after making it a single noun. Among the Arabs there are those who say "يا ابْنَ أُمِّي", keeping the yāʾ; the poet said:
؎يا ابْنَ أُمِّي ويا شُقَيِّقَ نَفْسِي ∗∗∗ أنْتَ خَلَّيْتَنِي لَدَهْرٍ شَدِيدِ
(O son of my mother, O dear brother of my soul, you have left me to a harsh fate.)

zajjaj:31-31.t:
And His saying — immediately after [the command to] cover oneself —: ﴿وَكُلُوا واشْرَبُوا﴾: because they claimed that Allah — exalted be His praise — had forbidden them something of what is in the bellies of livestock, and had forbidden them the baḥīra and the sāʾiba; and they used to claim, regarding the indecencies they committed, such as nakedness and the like, that Allah — exalted be His praise — had commanded them to do so. So Allah commanded them to cover themselves, and to eat what they claimed Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — had forbidden, though He had not forbidden it, and to drink of what they claimed Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — had forbidden them to drink, because the milk of the baḥīra and the sāʾiba was forbidden in their view.
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَلا تُسْرِفُوا إنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ المُسْرِفِينَ﴾. Excess (الإسْراف) is to eat what is not lawful to eat, of that of which Allah the Exalted has forbidden anything to be eaten, or that you eat of what He has made lawful for you beyond moderation and the measure of need. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that He does not love whoever is excessive; and whomever Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — does not love is in the Fire.

zajjaj:32-32.t: Then He made them acknowledge and rebuked them, saying: ﴿قُلْ مَن حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ﴾, i.e. who has forbidden that you wear in your circumambulation what covers you? ﴿والطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ﴾, i.e. and who has forbidden the good things of what Allah has provided? I.e. who has forbidden these things that you have stated to be forbidden? Then He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿قُلْ هي لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا خالِصَةً يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾; it is read "خالِصَةً" and "خالِصَةٌ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ". The meaning is that they are lawful for the believers, though the unbelievers may share them with them [in this world]; He — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the good things will be exclusively for the believers in the Hereafter, and no unbeliever will share them with them. As for the i'rab of "خالِصَةٌ", it is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, as you say "زَيْدٌ عاقِلٌ لَبِيبٌ (Zayd is intelligent, sagacious)"; the meaning is: "Say: they are established for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusive on the Day of Resurrection". Whoever reads "خالِصَةً" makes it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that the governing element is in your saying "في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا", in the sense of a ḥāl, as though you said: "They are established for the believers, settled in the life of this world, being exclusive on the Day of Resurrection".

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأنْ تُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَـزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطانًا﴾: the position of "أنْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "Allah has forbidden indecencies, [and] the forbidding of associating partners". The meaning of "لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطانًا" is: He has not sent down any proof for it.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أجَلٌ﴾, i.e. an appointed time. ﴿فَإذا جاءَ أجَلُهم لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ ساعَةً ولا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾: the meaning is "nor can they bring it forward an hour, nor less than an hour"; but the hour is mentioned because it is the smallest of the names of times.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
And His saying: ﴿يا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾: "آدَمُ" is a diptote (does not take tanwīn), because it is of the measure of "أفْعَلُ" and it is definite. It is derived from "أدَمَةِ الأرْضِ", which is the surface of the earth; so he was named after what he was created from — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best.
And His saying: ﴿إمّا يَأْتِيَنَّكم رُسُلٌ مِنكُمْ﴾: this is the "إنْ" of condition, to which "ما" has been joined. The original wording is "إنْ ما", separate, but it is assimilated, and it is written according to the assimilation. When "إنْ" is joined to "ما", the verb requires the heavy or the light nūn [of emphasis]. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition is in the fāʾ, i.e. in His saying: ﴿فَمَنِ اتَّقى وأصْلَحَ﴾. The nūn is required with "ما" only because "ما" enters as an emphasiser, so the nūn is required with it, just as the nūn is required with the lām in an oath when you say "واللَّهِ لَتَفْعَلَنَّ (By Allah, you shall surely do it)". So "ما" is emphasis just as the lām is emphasis, and the nūn became necessary just as it became necessary with the lām of the oath.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَمَن أظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾: what wrongdoing is more heinous than lying against Allah?! And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يَنالُهم نَصِيبُهم مِنَ الكِتابِ﴾, i.e. what Allah — exalted be His praise — has told of their recompense, as in His saying: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14], and His saying: ﴿يَسْلُكْهُ عَذابًا صَعَدًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 17], and His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُنافِقِينَ في الدَّرْكِ الأسْفَلِ مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 145], and like: ﴿إذِ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ والسَّلاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 71] ﴿فِي الحَمِيمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 72]. These are their portions from the Book, according to the measure of their sins in their unbelief. ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَتْهم رُسُلُنا﴾: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl claimed that "حَتّى", "أمّا" and "إلّا" do not admit imāla (inclining the alif towards ī). He does not allow "حَتِّي إذا جاءَتْهم", nor does he allow "أمِّا", nor "لِا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ"; all of this is a solecism (laḥn). He claimed that these are alifs of fatḥa, because they are the ends of particles that came for a meaning, so they were distinguished from the ends of nouns that contain alif, such as "حُبْلى" and "هُدى". Except that "حَتّى" is written with yāʾ because it has four letters, so it resembles "سَكْرى"; and "أمّا" of choice [i.e. إمّا] was likened to "إنْ" to which "ما" has been joined, as in His saying: ﴿إمّا أنْ تُعَذِّبَ وإمّا أنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 86], and it is written with alif for the reason we have described; and "إلّا" too is written with alif, because if it were written with yāʾ it would resemble "إلى".
And His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَتْهم رُسُلُنا يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ﴾: there are in it — and Allah knows best — two interpretations. It may be: "until, when the angels of death come to them to take them, they ask them at the moment of seeing [death], and at their death they recognise that they were unbelievers", because they said: ﴿أيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ قالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنّا﴾, i.e. they have come to nothing and gone.
It may also be — and Allah knows best — "until, when Our messengers, the angels of punishment, come to them to take them (يَتَوَفَّوْنَهم)", so that "يَتَوَفَّوْنَهم" in this place is of two kinds. One of them is "they take them in full by punishment", as you say "I have killed so-and-so with punishment" even if he did not die; the proof of this view is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَيَأْتِيهِ المَوْتُ مِن كُلِّ مَكانٍ وما هو بِمَيِّتٍ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 17]. And it is possible — and this is the weaker of the two interpretations — that they take their full number. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
And His saying: ﴿كُلَّما دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَها﴾: because they went astray, some of them by following others. ﴿حَتّى إذا ادّارَكُوا فِيها جَمِيعًا﴾, i.e. "تَدارَكُوا", the tāʾ being assimilated into the dāl. If you pause on His saying "حَتّى إذا", you cannot begin [again] without bringing the connecting alif, saying "اِدّارَكُوا"; you bring the connecting alif because the dāl in it is vowelless. The meaning of "تَدارَكُوا" is: they gathered together.
And His saying "جَمِيعًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "until, when they have overtaken one another in it, gathered together". ﴿قالَتْ أُخْراهم لأُولاهم رَبَّنا هَؤُلاءِ أضَلُّونا﴾, i.e. the last of them said [it]: the first of them called them, and the last followed the first; so the followers made known that those followed had led them astray by calling them to error. The meaning is: "The last of them said, 'O our Lord, these led us astray', of the first of them (لِأُولاهم)", meaning the first of them.
And His saying: ﴿فَآتِهِمْ عَذابًا ضِعْفًا مِنَ النّارِ﴾, i.e. a doubled punishment, because "الضِّعْف" in the speech of the Arabs is of two kinds: one is "the like (اَلْمِثْلُ)", and the other is in the sense of doubling the thing. ﴿قالَ لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ﴾, i.e. for the follower and the followed, because they all entered into unbelief, i.e. "for each a doubled punishment". Whoever reads ﴿وَلَكِنْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ with tāʾ [means]: "but you who are addressed do not know what punishment each party of you will have"; and whoever reads "وَلَكِنْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ" with yāʾ [means]: "but each party does not know the measure of the punishment of the other party". It may also be — and Allah knows best —: "but you do not know, O people of this world, the measure of that".

zajjaj:40-40.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا واسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها﴾, i.e. they denied Our proofs and Our signs which point to the prophethood of the prophets and the oneness of Allah. ﴿لا تُفَتَّحُ لَهم أبْوابُ السَّماءِ﴾, i.e. neither their souls nor their deeds ascend, because the deeds and souls of the believers ascend to heaven; Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ﴾ [Fāṭir: 10]. "لا تُفْتَحُ" and "لا تُفَتَّحُ" are both permissible, with the light and the doubled [tāʾ], and with yāʾ and with tāʾ. Some said: "لا تُفَتَّحُ لَهم أبْوابُ السَّماءِ" means the gates of the Garden, because the Garden is in heaven; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَلا يَدْخُلُونَ الجَنَّةَ﴾, so it is as though the gates of the Garden will not be opened for them and they will not enter it ﴿حَتّى يَلِجَ الجَمَلُ في سَمِّ الخِياطِ﴾. "اَلْخِياطُ" is the needle, and "سَمُّها" is its eye; the meaning is: "they will never enter the Garden".
