Ibn Masʿūd was asked about "الجَمَل", and he said: "It is the mate of the she-camel", as though he regarded whoever asked him about "الجَمَل" as ignorant. Some read "اَلْجُمَّلُ", and they explained it, saying: "the ship's hawser".
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُجْرِمِينَ﴾, i.e. "and like that which We have described do We recompense the criminals". "اَلْمُجْرِمُونَ" here — and Allah knows best — are the unbelievers, because what was mentioned of their story is the denial of the signs of Allah and arrogance towards them.

zajjaj:152-152.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا العِجْلَ سَيَنالُهم غَضَبٌ مِن رَبِّهِمْ وذِلَّةٌ﴾: the meaning is: they took the calf as a god.
His saying: ﴿وَذِلَّةٌ في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾: humiliation overtook them in that they saw that they had gone astray and been humbled. "اَلذِّلَّةُ" is what they were commanded of killing themselves. It has also been said that the humiliation is the taking of the jizya (poll-tax); but the taking of the jizya did not happen to those who worshipped the calf, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, accepted their repentance through their killing themselves.

zajjaj:154-154.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسى الغَضَبُ﴾: one says "سَكَتَ، يَسْكُتُ، سَكْتًا" when it subsides, and "سَكَتَ، يَسْكُتُ، سُكُوتًا، وسَكْتًا" when one stops speaking. One says "رَجُلٌ سِكِّيتٌ، بَيِّنُ السُّكُوتِ، والسّاكُوتَةِ" when he is often silent; and "أصابَ فُلانًا سُكّاتٌ" when an ailment has befallen him that prevents him from speaking; and "اَلسُّكَيْتُ", with the light and the doubled form, is the horse that comes last in a race. Some transmitted: "وَلَمّا سُكِتَ عَنْ مُوسى الغَضَبُ"; do not read it so, because it is contrary to the muṣḥaf.
Some said that "وَلَمّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسى الغَضَبُ" means: and when Moses fell silent from anger, by inversion (qalb), just as they said: "I put the cap into my head", meaning: I put my head into the cap. The view that its meaning is "subsided" is the view of the scholars of Arabic.

zajjaj:155-155.t:
His saying: ﴿واخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلا لِمِيقاتِنا﴾ means: and Moses chose from his people. Moses chose from the twelve tribes, six men from each tribe, and they reached seventy-two men, so he reduced them by two men. The meaning of "اِخْتارَ قَوْمَهُ" is "اِخْتارَ مِن قَوْمِهِ": "مِن" was omitted and the verb was connected (directly), so it governed the accusative. One says: "اِخْتَرْتُ مِنَ الرِّجالِ زَيْدًا" and "اِخْتَرْتُ الرِّجالَ زَيْدًا" (I chose Zayd from the men). And they recited:
؎وَمِنّا الَّذِي اخْتارَ الرِّجالَ سَماحَةً ∗∗∗ وجُودًا إذا هَبَّ الرِّياحُ الزَّعازِعُ
(And among us is he who was chosen from among the men for magnanimity and generosity, when the violent winds blow.)
His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا أخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾: it is violent movement, a violent earthquake. It is said that the mountain shook with them and they died. Then he said: ﴿رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أهْلَكْتَهم مِن قَبْلُ وإيّايَ﴾, that is: had You willed, You would have caused them to die before You brought upon them what made the quake fall due upon them.

zajjaj:156-156.t:
His saying: ﴿إنّا هُدْنا إلَيْكَ﴾ means: "we have turned in repentance to You". ﴿وَرَحْمَتِي وسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ means: everything I have created lives by My mercy and My grace; so its meaning is: "and My mercy encompasses everything in this world".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَسَأكْتُبُها لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾: in the Hereafter, that is: I will reward them with it in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:157-157.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الأُمِّيَّ﴾: "اَلْأُمِّيُّ" is one who remains in the natural state of the community (al-umma); he did not learn writing, so he is upon his innate disposition.
His saying: ﴿الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهم في التَّوْراةِ والإنْجِيلِ﴾: this is more conclusive as an argument against them, because it is information about what is in their own books, while the Prophet ﷺ did not write, did not read the Torah and the Gospel, and did not associate with their people. So his bringing what is in them is among the great signs of Allah. It is impossible that a claimant should come to a people and say to them "Mention of me is in your book" when it is not in it; and the mention of him informed those of the People of the Book who believed in him.
His saying: ﴿يَأْمُرُهم بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾: it is possible that "يَأْمُرُهم" is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
His saying: ﴿وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّباتِ﴾ means: he makes lawful for them the good foods that had been forbidden to them; and it may also be "وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّباتِ" in the sense of: whatever is taken in a good way, by its proper means. ﴿وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الخَبائِثَ ويَضَعُ عَنْهم إصْرَهُمْ﴾: "اَلْإصْرُ" is a heavy binding contract that you have tied. ﴿والأغْلالَ الَّتِي كانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: "اَلْأغْلالَ" (the shackles) is a figure of speech. Do you not see that you say "I have made this a collar around your neck" when there is no collar there? Its interpretation is only that I have entrusted this to you and obliged you to carry it out, so I made its being binding on you like a collar around your neck. And "the shackles that were upon them": it was imposed upon them that whoever killed was killed, no blood-money being accepted for that; and it was imposed upon them that when some urine touched their skin they had to cut it off; and it was imposed upon them that they not work on the Sabbath. These are the shackles that were upon them.
His saying: ﴿فالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ﴾ means: in Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَعَزَّرُوهُ ونَصَرُوهُ﴾: the lexicographers have differed about the meaning of His saying "وَعَزَّرُوهُ".
And the saying: "عَزَّرْتُ فُلانًا، أُعَزِّرُهُ، وأعْزُرُهُ، عَزْرًا": some said the meaning of "عَزَّرْتُهُ" is: I turned him back; some said the meaning of "عَزَّرْتُهُ" is: I came to his aid; some said: one says "عَزَّرْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أعْزِرُهُ" when I have blamed him. And one says "عَزَّرْتُ فُلانًا": some said "عَزَّرْتُ فُلانًا" means I helped him, and some said: "I defended him". So the meaning of "فالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وعَزَّرُوهُ ونَصَرُوهُ" is: the meaning of "عَزَّرُوهُ" is that they prevented his enemies from disbelieving in him. Some said: "عَزَّرُوهُ" means "نَصَرُوهُ" (they helped him), and the meaning is close, because defending him against enemies is helping him. And the meaning of "عَزَّرْتُ فُلانًا" is when I have beaten him with a beating below the ḥadd (prescribed penalty), preventing him by beating him from repeating the like of what he did.
And the saying "عَزَّرْتُهُ" meaning "I turned him back": "اَلتَّعْزِيرُ" (discretionary punishment) may come from it, that is: I did to him what turns him back from disobedience.
[Translator's note: "مَنَعْتُ مِنهُ" is rendered "I defended him" (literally "I protected [others] from him" / "I kept [harm] from him"); it is translated in the sense the following sentences give it. The forms "أعْزُرُهُ" and "أعْزِرُهُ" are as vowelled in the text.]
His saying: ﴿واتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْـزِلَ مَعَهُ﴾ means: and they followed the truth whose clarity in the hearts is like the clarity of light to the eyes.

zajjaj:159-159.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن قَوْمِ مُوسى أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالحَقِّ﴾ means: they call people to guidance by the truth, ﴿وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ means: and by the truth they judge.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
﴿لَهم مِن جَهَنَّمَ مِهادٌ﴾, i.e. a bed of fire; ﴿وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَواشٍ﴾, i.e. covering upon covering of fire.
And His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظّالِمِينَ﴾: the wrongdoers here are the unbelievers.
And His saying "غَواشٍ": Sībawayh and al-Khalīl both claimed that the tanwīn here is a compensation for the yāʾ, because "غَواشِيَ" is a diptote, and its original form is "غَواشِي" with the yāʾ vowelless; when the ḍamma goes, you bring in the tanwīn as a compensation for it. So the companions of Sībawayh explained it. Sībawayh held that the tanwīn is a compensation for the loss of the vowel of the yāʾ, and that the yāʾ dropped because it and the tanwīn were both vowelless. When you pause, the preferred course is to pause without yāʾ, saying "غَواشٍ", to show that the yāʾ used to be dropped in continuous speech. Some Arabs, when pausing, say "غَواشِي", retaining the yāʾ; but I do not consider that [acceptable] in the Qurʾān, because the yāʾ is omitted in the muṣḥaf, and the writing follows the pause.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ لا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إلا وُسْعَها﴾, i.e. they did righteous deeds according to the measure of their capacity, because the meaning of "اَلْوُسْعُ" is what one is able to do.
And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَنَّةِ هم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾: "أُولَئِكَ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), "أصْحابُ" is the khabar (predicate), and "هم" [too]; and the clause is the khabar of "اَلَّذِينَ", and the demonstrative — I mean "أُولَئِكَ" — refers back to "اَلَّذِينَ".

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَـزَعْنا ما في صُدُورِهِمْ مِن غِلٍّ﴾: some said: the rancours that were in their hearts have gone. Its reality — and Allah knows best — is that the people of the Garden will not envy one another for loftiness of rank, because envy is rancour (غِلّ).
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ الأنْهارُ﴾ is in the sense of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "And We removed whatever rancour was in their breasts, in this state". It may also be that "تَجْرِي" is a statement describing their condition, so that "تَجْرِي" is resumptive. The meaning of ﴿هَدانا لِهَذا﴾ is: "He guided us to what brought us to this". One says "هَدَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ هِدايَةً، وهُدًى، وهَدْيًا (I guided the man)", and "أهْدَيْتُ الهَدْيَةَ، فَهي مُهْداةٌ (I presented the gift, so it is presented)", and "أهْدَيْتُ العَرُوسَ إلى زَوْجِها، وهَدَيْتُها (I conducted the bride to her husband)".
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَنُودُوا أنْ تِلْكُمُ الجَنَّةُ﴾ is in the position of the accusative; here the hāʾ [pronoun] is implied, and [أنْ] is lightened from the heavy [أنَّ]; the meaning is: "they were called with [the announcement] that it is: that is the Garden (بِأنَّهُ تِلْكُمُ الجَنَّةُ)". The better view, in my opinion, is that "أنْ" is in the position of explaining the call, as if the meaning were: "And they were called: 'That is the Garden'", i.e. "it was said to them: that is the Garden". He said "تِلْكم" only because they were promised it in this world, so it is as though it were said: "This is that which you were promised". It is also possible that they saw it, and it was said to them before entering it, pointing to what they saw: "That is the Garden", as you say of what you see: "That man is your brother"; and if you said "This man", because he sees you, it would be permissible, because "هَذا" and "هَؤُلاءِ" are for what is near you, and "ذاكَ" and "تِلْكَ" for what is far from you, whether you see it or not.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَنادى أصْحابُ الجَنَّةِ أصْحابَ النّارِ أنْ قَدْ وجَدْنا ما وعَدَنا رَبُّنا حَقًّا﴾: the sense of "أنْ" here, if you wish, is explicative of what the people of the Garden called out, the meaning being: "that is (أيْ): we have found". It may also be the heavy "أنَّ", lightened, the meaning being: "that we have indeed found (أنَّهُ قَدْ وجَدْنا)". The poet said:
؎فِي فِتْيَةٍ كَسُيُوفِ الهِنْدِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا ∗∗∗ أنْ هالِكٌ كُلُّ مَن يَحْفى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among young men like Indian swords, who knew that everyone who goes barefoot or wears sandals must perish.)
And His saying: ﴿قالُوا نَعَمْ﴾: in some dialects, "قالُوا: نَعِمْ", in the sense of "نَعَمْ", with its end pausal, because it is a particle that came for a meaning.
And His saying: ﴿فَأذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهم أنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ﴾: "أنَّ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ" is permissible, and it has been read in both ways. The light one is lightened from the heavy one; and the light one may also be in the sense of the light "أيْ", which is explicative, as though it were an explanation of what they announced.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَنادى أصْحابُ الأعْرافِ﴾. People have differed about the people of al-Aʿrāf. Some said: "They are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they did not deserve the Garden by their good deeds, nor the Fire by their bad deeds"; so they were upon the barrier that is between the Garden and the Fire. "اَلْأعْرافُ" are the tops of the wall; everything high is called "عُرْفٌ", and its plural is "أعْرافٌ".
It may also be — and Allah knows best — that "عَلى الأعْرافِ" means: these men are in a state of recognising (مَعْرِفَة) the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire. Some said what we have mentioned, and that Allah will admit them into the Garden; some said: "the people of al-Aʿrāf" are prophets; and some said: angels. They recognise each by their mark: they recognise the people of the Garden in that their mark is the brightness of faces, laughter and rejoicing, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 38] ﴿ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 39]; and they recognise the people of the Fire by their mark, and their mark is the blackening of faces and their dustiness, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 106], and ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْها غَبَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 40] ﴿تَرْهَقُها قَتَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 41]; "اَلْقَتَرَةُ" is like smoke.
And His saying: ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْكم جَمْعُكم وما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾: this — and Allah knows best — is the address of the people of al-Aʿrāf to the people of the Fire. It has been read "تَسْتَكْثِرُونَ (you used to amass)" with thāʾ. As for His saying: ﴿أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمْتُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 49], He means the people of the Garden, as though it were said to them: "O people of the Fire, are these the ones about whom you swore ﴿لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 49]?" And if you wish, with fatḥa: "لا خَوْفَ عَلَيْكم". It is possible that "اُدْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ" is an address from the people of al-Aʿrāf to the people of the Garden, because everything the people of al-Aʿrāf say is from Allah the Exalted; and it is possible that it is an address from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — to the people of the Garden.
And His saying: ﴿وَنادى أصْحابُ النّارِ أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ أنْ أفِيضُوا عَلَيْنا مِنَ الماءِ أوْ مِمّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 50]: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the son of Adam is not independent of food and drink, even while being punished. And the people of the Garden informed them that Allah has forbidden them to the unbelievers, meaning that Allah has forbidden the food and drink of the people of the Garden to the people of the Fire, because they drink only the scalding water by which what is in their bellies is melted.

zajjaj:51-51.t:
And His saying: ﴿فاليَوْمَ نَنْساهم كَما نَسُوا لِقاءَ يَوْمِهِمْ هَذا﴾, i.e. We leave them in their punishment, as they left off working for the meeting of this Day of theirs. The meaning of ﴿وَما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ is "and as they denied (وَكَجَحْدِهِمْ)"; "ما" is conjoined (nasaq) to "كَما", in the position of the genitive.
And His saying: ﴿هُدًى ورَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 52]: "هُدًى" is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We set it out in detail as a guide and possessed of mercy". "هُدًى ورَحْمَةٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ" is also permissible, as a resumption, the meaning being: "It is guidance and mercy for a people who believe".

zajjaj:53-53.t:
And His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا تَأْوِيلَهُ﴾: its meaning is: "Do they await anything but that to which their affair will come (يَؤُولُ), namely the Resurrection?" This taʾwīl — and Allah knows best — is [the one in] His saying: ﴿وَما يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إلا اللَّهُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 7], i.e. none knows when the Resurrection will be, and what it will lead to, except Allah; ﴿والرّاسِخُونَ في العِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنّا بِهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 7], [i.e.] in the Resurrection — and Allah knows best.
And His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: "يَوْمَ" is accusative by His saying "يَقُولُ". And "اَلَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ" is of two kinds: it is possible that in turning away from it they became like one who has forgotten; and it is possible that they [actually] forgot it and abandoned working for it and believing in it.
And His saying: ﴿أوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنّا نَعْمَلُ﴾: "أوْ" is conjoined (nasaq) to His saying "مِن شُفَعاءَ", as though they said: "Is there an intercessor who will intercede for us? Or will we be sent back?"
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَنَعْمَلَ﴾ is accusative as the answer with the fāʾ to the interrogative. "أوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ" may also be put in the accusative [i.e. "أوْ نُرَدَّ"], meaning: "If we were sent back, we would have no need of intercession".

zajjaj:54-54.t: And His saying: ﴿يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ﴾ and "يُغَشِّي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ" — it is read in both ways. The meaning is that the night comes upon the day and covers it. He did not say "and He covers the night with the day (يُغْشِي النَّهارَ اللَّيْلَ)", because there is an indication of it in the speech; and it has come elsewhere: ﴿يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلى النَّهارِ ويُكَوِّرُ النَّهارَ عَلى اللَّيْلِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 5]. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّراتٍ بِأمْرِهِ﴾, i.e. He created the stars running their courses by His command.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
And His saying: ﴿ادْعُوا رَبَّكم تَضَرُّعًا وخُفْيَةً﴾: some said: "تَضَرَّعُوا" means: be supplicating (تَمَلَّقُوا). Its reality — and Allah knows best — is that they call upon Him humbly, in worship. And "خُفْيَةً", i.e. hold His worship firmly within yourselves, because supplication (الدُّعاء) means worship.
And His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ المُعْتَدِينَ﴾: "اَلْمُعْتَدُونَ" are those who go beyond what they were commanded, and they are the wrongdoers.

zajjaj:160-160.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَطَّعْناهُمُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أسْباطًا﴾; "عَشِرَةَ" with kasra on the shīn is also permissible. The meaning is: We divided them into twelve groups, أسْباطًا, as a naʿt (adjective) of "فِرْقَةً" (group); as though He said: "We made them tribes, and We divided them into tribes", so "أسْباطًا" is a badal (substitute) for "اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ", and this is the (correct) way.
His saying "أُمَمًا" is a naʿt of "أسْباطًا".
Some said: "اَلسِّبْطُ" is the generation that comes after a generation. The correct view is that the asbāṭ among the descendants of Isaac are in the position of the qabāʾil (tribes) among the descendants of Ishmael: the offspring of each of the sons of Jacob is a sibṭ, and the offspring of each of the descendants of Ishmael is a qabīla. These were called asbāṭ and those qabāʾil only to distinguish between the descendants of Ishmael and the descendants of Isaac. The meaning of "اَلْقَبِيلَةُ" among the descendants of Ishmael is the meaning of "اَلْجَماعَةُ" (group): every group of offspring is called "قَبِيلَةٌ", and likewise every assembly gathered on one thing is called "قَبِيلٌ"; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إنَّهُ يَراكم هو وقَبِيلُهُ مِن حَيْثُ لا تَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 27].
As for al-asbāṭ, it is derived from "اَلسَّبَطُ"; "اَلسُّبَطُ" is a kind of tree which camels are fed; and one says of a tree: "it has qabāʾil (branches)". So likewise al-asbāṭ is from "اَلسَّبَطُ", as though He made Isaac like a tree and made Ishmael like a tree. Genealogists do the same in genealogy: they make the father like a tree and make the children like its branches; and one says: "Blessed is the offshoot of so-and-so", and "So-and-so is from a righteous tree". This, and Allah knows best, is the meaning of "اَلْأسْباطُ" and "اَلسِّبْطُ".
[Translator's note: the plant name is vowelled first "اَلسَّبَطُ" and then "اَلسُّبَطُ" in the text; both are kept as written.]

zajjaj:163-163.t:
His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿واسْألْهم عَنِ القَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كانَتْ حاضِرَةَ البَحْرِ إذْ يَعْدُونَ في السَّبْتِ﴾: questioning is of two kinds. One of the two kinds is that you ask to be informed about what you do not know, in order to know. The second kind is that you ask seeking information by way of making someone admit (taqrīr), so you say to a man: "Did I do such-and-such?", while you know that you did not do it; you only ask him to make him admit and to rebuke him.
[Translator's note: the example is translated as written; the point of a taqrīr question would more naturally be served by something like "Did you do such-and-such?" while knowing he did.]
So the meaning of commanding the Prophet ﷺ to ask the People of the Book about the people of this town (when Allah, exalted be His praise, had already related its story) is to make them admit their long-standing disbelief, and to inform them of what can only be known through a scripture or revelation.
﴿إذْ يَعْدُونَ في السَّبْتِ﴾ means: when they transgressed on the Sabbath. One says: "عَدا فُلانٌ، يَعْدُو، عُدْوانًا، وعِداءً، وعَدْوًا، وعُدُوًّا" when he does wrong.
His saying: ﴿إذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتانُهم يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ﴾: "حِيتانٌ" is the plural of "حُوتٌ"; the Arabs most often call fish "اَلْحِيتانَ" and "اَلنِّينانِ".
﴿إذْ يَعْدُونَ في السَّبْتِ﴾: the position of "إذْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "Ask them about their transgressing on the Sabbath", that is: ask them about the time of that. "إذْ تَأتِيهِمْ" is also in the position of the accusative, governed by "يَعْدُونَ"; the meaning is: ask them about when they transgressed at the time of (the fish) coming. ﴿شُرَّعًا﴾ means: appearing openly. The fish used to come openly, so they would use a stratagem of penning them in on the Sabbath and then taking them on Sunday. It is also said that they openly took them on the Sabbath.
His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَبْلُوهُمْ﴾ means: with the like of this severe trial We try them. The position of the kāf is accusative, governed by His saying: ﴿نَبْلُوهم بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾, that is: I made the trial severe for them because of their transgression. It is possible, though far-fetched, that it is: ﴿وَيَوْمَ لا يَسْبِتُونَ لا تَأْتِيهِمْ كَذَلِكَ﴾, that is: they do not come to them openly (in that manner), and "نَبْلُوهم" is then resumptive. The first view is the view of the people, and it is the good one.

zajjaj:164-164.t:
﴿وَإذْ قالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنهم لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْمًا﴾: the origin is "لِما", but the alif is dropped with the prepositions, as in "لِمَ", "عَمَّ" and "بِمَ"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 54], ﴿عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 1]. The meaning of the verse is that they blamed them for admonishing a people who they knew would not desist; this was what predominated in their knowledge of them. ﴿اللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهم أوْ مُعَذِّبُهم عَذابًا شَدِيدًا﴾: the meaning of "أوْ" (or), and Allah knows best, is that they informed them, according to what they had seen of their deeds, that they would inevitably be destroyed in this world or punished in the Hereafter.
His saying: ﴿قالُوا مَعْذِرَةً إلى رَبِّكُمْ﴾: the meaning is: they said: our admonishing them is an excuse (presented) to your Lord. ﴿وَلَعَلَّهم يَتَّقُونَ﴾: so the meaning is that they said: commanding what is right is obligatory upon us, so it is upon us to admonish these people, that perhaps they may be God-fearing; that is: and it is possible in our view that they will benefit from the excuse.
The accusative is also permissible in "مَعْذِرَةً", and then the meaning of His saying "قالُوا مَعْذِرَةً إلى رَبِّكم" is in the sense of "they offer an excuse (يَعْتَذِرُونَ مَعْذِرَةً)".
[Translator's note: the text as quoted already has "مَعْذِرَةً" in the accusative; the discussion implies that the reading first explained is the nominative "مَعْذِرَةٌ" (with an omitted subject: "our admonition is an excuse").]

zajjaj:165-165.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَمّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ﴾: "نَسُوا" may be in the sense of "تَرَكُوا" (they abandoned), and it may be that their abandoning was like that of one who forgot.
His saying: ﴿أنْجَيْنا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُّوءِ وأخَذْنا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ﴾ means: severe. One says: "بَئِسَ، يَبْؤُسُ، بَأْسًا" when it became severe.
It was said that the people were three groups: a group that did evil, a group that forbade evil, and a group that refrained from forbidding. It was also said that they were two groups: a group that forbade evil and a group that did evil; and some of the group among whom were those who forbade evil were believers not pleased with what the people of evil did, so they were included in the rescue with those who forbade evil, and the punishment descended on those who transgressed on the Sabbath.

zajjaj:166-166.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا عَتَوْا عَنْ ما نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾: "اَلْعاتِي" is one deeply immersed in corruption, the rebel who accepts no admonition.
His saying: ﴿قُلْنا لَهم كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خاسِئِينَ﴾: it is possible that they were commanded to become so by a saying that was heard, which would be more conclusive as a sign and as a calamity befalling them; and it is possible that "فَقُلْنا لَهم" is of the kind of His saying: ﴿إنَّما أمْرُهُ إذا أرادَ شَيْئًا أنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 82]. The meaning of "خاسِئِينَ" is: driven away.
Some people said: it is possible that these apes which breed have their origin from them. Others said: the transformed do not survive and do not breed. In sum, we have been informed that they were made apes, and apes are those we know, which are the animals most resembling the son of Adam; and Allah knows best how their affair went after their becoming apes.

zajjaj:167-167.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ تَأذَّنَ رَبُّكَ﴾: some said: "تَأذَّنَ" means: your Lord swore, ﴿لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (that He would surely send against them). It was also said that "تَأذَّنَ" means: He made known; the Arabs say "تَعَلَّمْ أنَّ هَذا كَذا" in the sense of "اِعْلَمْ" (know that this is so). Zuhayr said:
؎تَعَلَّمْ أنَّ شَرَّ النّاسِ حَيٌّ ∗∗∗ يُنادِي في شِعارِهِمُ يَسارُ
(Know that the worst of people is a clan whose battle-cry calls out "Yasār".)
And Zuhayr also said:
؎فَقُلْتُ تَعَلَّمْ أنَّ لِلصَّيْدِ غِرَّةً ∗∗∗ وإلّا ∗∗∗ تُضَيِّعْها فَإنَّكَ قاتِلُهُ
(So I said: know that the game has a moment of unwariness, and if you do not waste it, you will kill it.)
[Translator's note: the verse is printed with an extra divider "∗∗∗" inside the second hemistich; it is kept as in the text.]
His saying: ﴿لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ مَن يَسُومُهم سُوءَ العَذابِ﴾ means: someone who will inflict upon them the worst of punishment.
If someone says: they were made apes, so how will they remain until the Day of Resurrection? The meaning is that the mention is of the Jews: some of them were transformed, and apes and swine were made of them, and those who remained are obstinate against the command of Allah; so they are humiliated by being killed unless they pay the jizya, and then they are humiliated by it; and in every place they are the most humiliated of its people. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ أيْنَ ما ثُقِفُوا إلا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وحَبْلٍ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 112], that is: unless they are given protection (dhimma) and a covenant.

zajjaj:169-169.t:
His saying: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ ورِثُوا الكِتابَ﴾: that which comes in the wake of a generation is called "خَلْفٌ" (successors). And "اَلْخَلْفُ" is what is given back to you as a replacement for what was taken from you, and "خَلْفٌ" is also said in this sense; but as for what is given back to you as a replacement for what has gone from you, it is "اَلْخَلَفُ", with fatḥa on the lām.
[Translator's note: the text first says "اَلْخَلْفُ" (sukūn) is the replacement and then that the replacement is "اَلْخَلَفُ" (fatḥa); it is translated as written.]
His saying: ﴿وَرِثُوا الكِتابَ يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَذا الأدْنى﴾: it was said that they used to take bribes for judgements and judge unjustly; and it was said that they used to take bribes and judge rightly; and all of that is a base worldly gain.
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنا وإنْ يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ﴾: the point is that they sinned by taking bribes and said "we will be forgiven" without repenting, because His saying ﴿وَإنْ يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ﴾ is evidence of their persistence in sin; while Allah, Majestic and Mighty, promised forgiveness for the enormities that entail the Fire only with repentance. So He said: ﴿ألَمْ يُؤْخَذْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِيثاقُ الكِتابِ أنْ لا يَقُولُوا عَلى اللَّهِ إلا الحَقَّ ودَرَسُوا ما فِيهِ﴾, that is: they are mindful of what was taken from them as a pledge.

zajjaj:170-170.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِالكِتابِ وأقامُوا الصَّلاةَ إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ المُصْلِحِينَ﴾: "اَلَّذِينَ" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ). There are two views on it, I mean on "إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ المُصْلِحِينَ" (as its predicate). Some said: (it means) "We do not let the reward of the righteous among them be lost", and this is what we choose, because whoever is not a believer and does righteous deeds, his reward is void. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1], and He said: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خاشِعَةٌ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 2] ﴿عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 3] ﴿تَصْلى نارًا حامِيَةً﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 4]. So the meaning is: "And those who hold fast to the Book", that is, believe in it and judge by what is in it, "We do not let the reward of the righteous one among them be lost"; and the righteous one is the one who remains steadfast in faith and fulfils its obligations in belief and practice. Similar to it is: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ مَن أحْسَنَ عَمَلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 30], that is: We do not let the reward of whoever among them does good deeds be lost.
Others said: "اَلْمُصْلِحُونَ" is a word differing from the wording of the first (الَّذِينَ), but its meaning is the meaning of the first, so the referent (al-dhikr) returns in meaning even though it does not return in wording. These people do not allow "زَيْدٌ قامَ أبُو عَمْرٍو" (Zayd, Abū ʿAmr stood), because the word "زَيْدٌ" does not entail Abū ʿAmr.
If someone says: "اَلْمُؤْمِنُ أنا أُكْرِمُ مَنِ اتَّقى اللَّهَ" (the believer: I honour whoever fears Allah), it is permissible, because the meaning of "مَنِ اتَّقى اللَّهَ" is the meaning of "اَلْمُؤْمِنُ"; so it has become like your saying "زَيْدٌ ضَرَبْتُهُ" (Zayd, I struck him), because when the referent has preceded, the hāʾ inevitably refers back to it, even though its wording is not its wording, since the pronoun of the absent person in the accusative can only be a "hāʾ".

zajjaj:172-172.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ أخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ﴾: the position of "إذْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "And remember when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs". "مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ" is a badal (substitute) for His saying "مِن بَنِي آدَمَ". The meaning is: "And when your Lord took their offspring and their offsprings, all of them".
His saying: ﴿وَأشْهَدَهم عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ ألَسْتُ بِرَبِّكم قالُوا بَلى﴾: some said: Allah created people like tiny ants (dharr) from the loins of Adam and made them testify to His oneness. It is possible that He gave the likes of tiny ants an understanding by which they comprehend His command, just as He said: ﴿قالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يا أيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Naml: 18], and as He said: ﴿وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 79]; and «Every child is born upon the fiṭra (natural disposition) — its meaning is that he is born with the oneness of Allah in his heart — until his parents are the ones who make him a Jew or make him a Christian».
Others said: its meaning is that Allah, exalted be His praise, brought forth the children of Adam, some of them from the backs of others; and the meaning of ﴿وَأشْهَدَهم عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ ألَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾ is that every mature person knows that Allah is One, because everything that Allah the Exalted created is evidence of His oneness. They said: were it not for that, there would be no argument against the disbeliever. They said: so the meaning of "وَأشْهَدَهم عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ ألَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ؟" is: He guided them by His creation to His oneness.

zajjaj:175-175.t:
His saying: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ الَّذِي آتَيْناهُ آياتِنا فانْسَلَخَ مِنها﴾: this is conjoined (nasaq) to what precedes it; the meaning is: "Recite to them (the account of) when your Lord took from the children of Adam, and recite to them the account of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he cast them off". There is more than one view on this. It was said that he possessed the greatest name of Allah and invoked it against Moses and his companions. It was said that he was Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt, who had knowledge from the scriptures. And it was said that the hypocrites among the People of the Book are meant by it.
His saying: ﴿فَكانَ مِنَ الغاوِينَ﴾ means: of the corrupt who perish.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
And His saying: ﴿وادْعُوهُ خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا﴾, i.e. call upon Him fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No one will enter the Garden by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah envelops me in His mercy." And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾: "قَرِيبٌ" (masculine) was said only because mercy (الرَّحْمَة) and forgiveness (الغُفْران) have one meaning; and likewise every feminine that is not a true feminine. Al-Akhfash said: it is possible that "الرَّحْمَة" here is in the sense of rain.
Some said: this [masculine form] was used to distinguish "اَلْقَرِيبُ" from "اَلْقَرابَةُ (kinship)" and "اَلْقَرِيبُ" from "اَلْقُرْبُ (nearness)". This is a mistake, because everything that is near in place or in lineage follows whatever feminine or masculine [agreement] befalls it.

zajjaj:57-57.t:
And His saying: ﴿بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾, and also "نُشْرًا", with ḍamma on the nūn, and with its fatḥa; and ʿĀṣim read "بُشْرًا" with bāʾ. Whoever reads "نَشْرًا", the meaning is: "And He is the One who spreads the winds, spread out, a spreading (نَشْرًا)". Whoever says "نُشْرًا", it is the plural of "نُشُورٌ", [i.e.] "نُشُرٌ". Whoever reads "بُشْرًا", it is the plural of "بَشِيرَةٌ", [i.e.] "بُشُرٌ", as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّياحَ بُشْرًا﴾.
And His saying: ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾, i.e. ahead of the rain, which is a mercy. ﴿حَتّى إذا أقَلَّتْ سَحابًا﴾, i.e. "until, when the wind has borne up clouds". One says "أقَلَّ فُلانٌ الشَّيْءَ" when he carries it, and "so-and-so cannot manage (لا يَسْتَقِلُّ) to carry it". So the meaning is: "until, when it has carried heavy clouds". "اَلسَّحابُ" is the plural of "سَحابَةٌ". ﴿ثِقالا﴾, i.e. heavy with water. ﴿سُقْناهُ لِبَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ﴾, and "مَيْتٍ" — both [are read]. ﴿فَأنْـزَلْنا بِهِ الماءَ فَأخْرَجْنا بِهِ مِن كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ﴾: it may be "so We sent down water by the clouds, and brought forth by it every kind of fruit"; the better — and Allah knows best — is "and brought forth by the water every kind of fruit". And it may be "We brought forth by the land every kind of fruit", because "البَلَد" here does not single out one land apart from all other lands.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نُخْرِجُ المَوْتى﴾, i.e. "like that bringing forth to which We have pointed, We shall bring forth the dead".
And His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّكم تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: "لَعَلَّ" expresses hope (tarajjī). The servants are addressed only according to the measure of their knowledge, and what some of them hope from others; and Allah knows whether they will take heed or not.
And His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّكم تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾, i.e. perhaps by what We have made clear to you, you will infer the oneness of Allah, and that He resurrects the dead.

zajjaj:58-58.t: And His saying: ﴿والبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ يَخْرُجُ نَباتُهُ بِإذْنِ رَبِّهِ والَّذِي خَبُثَ لا يَخْرُجُ إلا نَكِدًا﴾. The people of Medina read it "نَكَدًا", with fatḥa on the kāf. Two other forms are possible in it: "إلّا نَكْدًا", and "نُكْدًا" with ḍamma on the nūn and the kāf vowelless; but the one with ḍamma is not to be read, because no transmission of it in the Qurʾān is established.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
And His saying ﴿قالَ المَلأُ مِن قَوْمِهِ﴾: they are the chiefs and the nobles; and some said: the men are meant by it. We have explained "اَلْمَلَأُ" earlier in the book.
And His saying: ﴿أوَعَجِبْتُمْ أنْ جاءَكم ذِكْرٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 63]: this wāw is the wāw of conjunction, onto which the interrogative alif has entered, so it has remained with fatḥa; we have explained it in the book.
And His saying: ﴿فِي الفُلْكِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 64]: "اَلْفُلْكُ" is the ship; "اَلْفُلْكُ" may be singular and may be plural.
And His saying: ﴿قَوْمًا عَمِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 64], i.e. they had become blind to the truth and to faith.

zajjaj:65-65.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإلى عادٍ أخاهم هُودًا﴾: the meaning is: "We sent Noah to his people, and We sent to ʿĀd their brother Hūd". The prophets are called "their brother" even though they [the people] were unbelievers, meaning that a human being like them, of the offspring of their father Adam, came to them, and this is more compelling against them. And it is possible that [he is called] "their brother" because he was of their people, so that it would be more intelligible to them to take [the message] from a man among them.

zajjaj:66-66.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنّا لَنَراكَ في سَفاهَةٍ﴾: "اَلسَّفاهَةُ" is lightness of forbearance and judgement; one says "ثَوْبٌ سَفِيهٌ" when a garment is flimsy.
And His saying: ﴿وَإنّا لَنَظُنُّكَ مِنَ الكاذِبِينَ﴾: they disbelieved in him on the basis of supposition, not certainty.

zajjaj:67-67.t:
And His saying: ﴿يا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي سَفاهَةٌ﴾: this is a place of instruction in manners for people in good conduct of discussion and address: he repelled the folly they attributed to him by saying "there is no folly in me", repelling them only by denying what they said.
And His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾, i.e. what I inform you of is from Allah; for he commanded them to worship Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — and to affirm His oneness.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
And His saying: ﴿واذْكُرُوا إذْ جَعَلَكم خُلَفاءَ مِن بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وزادَكم في الخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً﴾: "خُلَفاءُ" is the plural of "خَلِيفَةٌ" according to the [masculine] gender [of the referent], not according to the form, like "ظَرِيفٌ" and "ظُرَفاءُ".
It may also be pluralised as "خَلائِفُ", according to the form, like "طَرِيفَةٌ" and "طَرائِفُ".
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَزادَكم في الخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً﴾: in the exegesis [it is said] that the shortest of them was sixty cubits tall and the tallest a hundred cubits.
And His saying: ﴿فاذْكُرُوا آلاءَ اللَّهِ﴾: its meaning is "the favours of Allah"; its singular is "إلًى". The poet said:
؎أبْيَضُ لا يَرْهَبُ الهُزالَ ولا ∗∗∗ يَقْطَعُ رِحْمًا ولا يَخُونُ إلّا
(A man of pure honour, who fears no leanness [of want], who does not sever kinship, nor betray a favour (إلًى).)
Its singular may also be "إلْيٌ" and "إلًى".

zajjaj:73-73.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإلى ثَمُودَ أخاهم صالِحًا﴾, i.e. We sent to Thamūd their brother Ṣāliḥ. "ثَمُودُ" in the Book of Allah is both declinable with tanwīn (maṣrūf) and a diptote. The declinable one is His saying: "ألا إنَّ ثَمُودًا كَفَرُوا رَبَّهم ألا بُعْدًا لِّثَمُودَ", the second being a diptote. Whoever declines it fully makes it a name for the tribe-as-group (الحَيّ), so it is masculine — a masculine thing named by it; and whoever does not decline it fully makes it a name for the tribe (القَبِيلَة).
And His saying: ﴿ما لَكم مِن إلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ﴾, also read "غَيْرِهِ". Whoever puts it in the nominative, the meaning is "you have no god other than Him (ما لَكم إلَهٌ غَيْرُهُ)", and "مِن" entered as an emphasiser; whoever puts it in the genitive makes it a naʿt (adjective) of "إلَهٍ". Some allowed the accusative in "غَيْرُ"; it is permissible outside the Qurʾān, as accusative of exception, or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun; but it is not permissible in the Qurʾān, because it has not been read so. Al-Farrāʾ allowed "ما جاءَنِي غَيْرَكَ (no one came to me but you)" with "غَيْرَ" in the accusative; this is a clear error. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh only recited a verse in which they allowed the accusative of "غَيْرَ", and he cited that verse as evidence and was misled by the wording, while the two of them said that the position is one of the nominative. "غَيْرَ" in the verse is only annexed to something not fully declinable, so it was made indeclinable on fatḥa, just as "يَوْمَ" is made indeclinable on fatḥa when annexed to "إذٍ". The verse is the poet's saying:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing kept her from drinking from it but that a dove cooed among branches laden with fruit.)
Most of them recite it "غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ": when he annexed "غَيْرَ" to "أنْ", he gave "غَيْرَ" fatḥa. But if you said "ما جاءَنِي غَيْرَكَ", it would not be permissible; and if this were permissible, "ما جاءَنِي زَيْدًا" would be permissible.
And His saying: ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾: he called them to the affirmation of oneness, and pointed them to his prophethood by the she-camel, saying: ﴿هَذِهِ ناقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكم آيَةً﴾. "آيَةً" is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "look at this she-camel as a sign", i.e. a token. There has been disagreement about her story. It was said in some exegesis that the chiefs of Ṣāliḥ's people were in front of him and asked him for a sign, and there was before him a ṣafāh — that is, a smooth rock — and Allah brought forth from it a she-camel together with her saqb, i.e. her calf. And it has come in some exegesis that he took a she-camel from among the other she-camels, and Allah gave her a day's share of drinking and them a day's share of drinking. Her story is mentioned elsewhere, where He said: ﴿هَذِهِ ناقَةٌ لَها شِرْبٌ ولَكم شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 155]. She would drink one day, then on the next day she would stand straddling in a valley, and she would go on being milked, and her milking would not cease that day. So it is possible that the matter of her emerging from the rock is true, and it is possible that the matter of her milking is true, and each of them is a miraculous sign pointing to prophethood; and it is possible that both reports are true, so that it is combined that she came out of a rock and that her milking was as we have mentioned. He would not have said ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ so that it would be a sign containing ambiguity.
And His saying: ﴿واذْكُرُوا إذْ جَعَلَكم خُلَفاءَ مِن بَعْدِ عادٍ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 74], i.e. when He destroyed them and made you inherit the land. ﴿وَبَوَّأكم في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 74], i.e. He settled you. The poet said:
؎وَبُوِّئَتْ في صَمِيمِ مَعْشَرِها ∗∗∗ وتَمَّ في قَوْمِها مُبَوَّؤُها
(She was settled in the very heart of her clan, and her settling-place among her people was complete.)
I.e. she was settled, in nobility, in the purest lineage.
And His saying: ﴿وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الجِبالِ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 149]: one says "نَحَتَ، يَنْحِتُ (to carve)", and one also says "نَحَتَ، يَنْحَتُ", because it contains one of the guttural letters. It is related that because of the length of their lives they needed to carve houses in the mountains, because roofs and buildings would decay before their lives came to an end.

zajjaj:176-176.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَرَفَعْناهُ بِها﴾ means: had We willed to come between him and disobedience, We would have done so. ﴿وَلَكِنَّهُ أخْلَدَ إلى الأرْضِ﴾ means: but he inclined to this world and settled in it. One says "أخْلَدَ فُلانٌ إلى كَذا وكَذا" and "خَلَدَ إلى كَذا وكَذا", and "أخْلَدَ" is more frequent in the language. The meaning is that he settled into the pleasures of the earth and followed his desire; that is: He did not raise him by them, because of his following his desire.
His saying: ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الكَلْبِ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, struck for the one who abandons His signs and turns away from them the most fitting parable, in the vilest of his states. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الكَلْبِ﴾ when the dog is panting. That is because when the dog is panting, it is able to do neither harm nor benefit for itself; for the comparison with it is on the basis that it pants in every state, whether you drive it off or leave it alone. So the meaning is: his likeness is as the likeness of the dog panting. Then He said: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَثَلُ القَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾ (that is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs).

zajjaj:177-177.t: And He said: ﴿ساءَ مَثَلا القَوْمُ﴾: the meaning is: evil as a likeness is the likeness of the people.

zajjaj:179-179.t:
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ كالأنْعامِ بَلْ هم أضَلُّ﴾: He described them as not seeing with their eyes and not understanding with their hearts; He made them, in their abandoning the truth and turning away from it, like one who neither sees nor understands. Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿بَلْ هم أضَلُّ﴾ (rather, they are further astray); that is because cattle perceive what benefits and what harms them, so they keep to some of what they do not perceive, while most of these people know that they are obstinate and yet rush headlong into the Fire. And He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَما أصْبَرَهم عَلى النّارِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 175], that is: (how patient they are) in the deeds of the people of the Fire.
[Translator's note: "فَتَلْزَمُ بَعْضَ ما لا تُبْصِرُهُ" is translated as written; the sense may be "and so keep away from what they do not see (clearly)".]

zajjaj:180-180.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى فادْعُوهُ بِها﴾: no one should call upon Him by what He has not described Himself with, or has not named Himself with. So one says in supplication: "يا اَللَّهُ يا رَحْمَنُ يا جَوادُ" (O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Most Generous), but one should not say "يا سُبْحانَ", because He did not describe Himself with this word. You say "يا رَحِيمُ" but you do not say "يا رَفِيقُ"; and you say "يا قَوِيُّ" but you do not say "يا جَلْدُ" (O hardy one).

zajjaj:185-185.t:
His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا في مَلَكُوتِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾ means: have they not drawn inferences from what He told them of the dominion of the heavens and the earth?! ﴿وَأنْ عَسى أنْ يَكُونَ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ أجَلُهُمْ﴾ means: if they are putting off repentance, then perhaps their term has drawn near. So the meaning is: "Have they not looked into that by which Allah, exalted be His praise, has guided them to His oneness?! Yet they disbelieved in Him despite that; and perhaps their terms have drawn near, so they will die in disbelief". ﴿فَبِأيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (then in what discourse after it will they believe?).
His saying: ﴿وَيَذَرُهم في طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]: "اَلطُّغْيانُ" is excess in disbelief, and "يَعْمَهُونَ" means: they wander in confusion. Both the jussive (jazm) and the nominative (rafʿ) are permissible in "يَذَرُهم". Whoever puts it in the jussive conjoins it to the position of the fāʾ (i.e. the apodosis); the meaning is: "Whomever Allah leads astray, He leaves him in his transgression, wandering blindly". Whoever reads "وَيَذَرُهم" has it nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf).

zajjaj:187-187.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ السّاعَةِ أيّانَ مُرْساها﴾: "اَلسّاعَةُ" here is the Hour in which creation dies. The meaning of "مُرْساها" is: its fixing. One says "رَسا الشَّيْءُ، يَرْسُو" when it is firmly fixed, so it is "راسٍ"; likewise "جِبالٌ راسِياتٌ", that is: firmly fixed; and "أرْسَيْتُهُ" when I have fixed it. So the meaning is: "They ask you about the Hour: when will it occur?".
His saying: ﴿لا يُجَلِّيها لِوَقْتِها إلا هُوَ﴾ means: none but He will make it appear at its time.
As for the meaning of ﴿ثَقُلَتْ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, two views have been stated about it. Some said: "ثَقُلَتْ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ" means its occurrence weighs heavily on the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. Then He, exalted be His praise, made known how it would occur, and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لا تَأْتِيكم إلا بَغْتَةً﴾, that is: only suddenly.
[Translator's note: only the first of the two announced views is given in the text.]
His saying: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ كَأنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْها﴾: the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: they ask you about it as though you were delighted with their asking. One says "تَحَفَّيْتُ بِفُلانٍ فِي المَسْألَةِ" when I asked a question in which I showed affection and kindness towards him. And "أحْفى فُلانٌ بِفُلانٍ في المَسْألَةِ": its interpretation is only abundance (persistence in asking). One says "حَفِتِ الدّابَّةُ، تَحْفى، حَفًى", with the short ending (maqṣūr), when the walking has been so much that it hurts it; and "اَلْحِفاءُ", with the long ending (mamdūd), is for a man to walk without sandals. It was also said: "كَأنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْها" means: as though you had asked much about it.
His saying: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning of "إنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ اللَّهِ" is: none knows it but He.

zajjaj:188-188.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ كُنْتُ أعْلَمُ الغَيْبَ لاسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ الخَيْرِ﴾ means: I would have stored up in the time of plenty for the time of drought. It was also said: "لَوْ كُنْتُ أعْلَمُ الغَيْبَ" means: "If I knew what I am asked about of the unseen concerning the Hour and other things…".
His saying: ﴿وَما مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ﴾ means: no denial would have overtaken me. It was also said: "وَما مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ" means: "there is no madness in me", because they attributed madness to the Prophet ﷺ, so he said: ﴿وَما مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ إنْ أنا إلا نَذِيرٌ وبَشِيرٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَعَتَوْا عَنْ أمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, i.e. they exceeded the limit in unbelief. ﴿فَأخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 78]: "اَلرَّجْفَةُ" is the violent earthquake. It is related that when he said to them: ﴿تَمَتَّعُوا في دارِكم ثَلاثَةَ أيّامٍ﴾ [Hūd: 65], on the first day they awoke with their faces yellow, on the second day with their faces red, on the third day with their faces black, and on the fourth day the punishment came upon them. It is said that the beginning of their hamstringing of the she-camel was on Wednesday, and the punishment seized them on Saturday.
And His saying: ﴿فَأصْبَحُوا نادِمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 157], i.e. at a time when regret would not benefit them; and "فَأصْبَحُوا جاثِمِينَ (and they became prostrate)" on the day on which the earthquake seized them. The meaning of "جاثِمِينَ" is: they had become extinct from the severity of the punishment. Some said: they became like settled ashes.

zajjaj:80-80.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلُوطًا إذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أتَأْتُونَ الفاحِشَةَ﴾, i.e. and We sent Lot, when he said to his people. Al-Akhfash said: it may also be accusative on [the implied sense] "and mention Lot, when he said to his people". The proper view is that it is conjoined to the sending. One of the lexicographers said: "لُوطٌ" is derived from "لِطْتُ الحَوْضَ (I plastered the basin)", when I have smoothed it with clay. This is a mistake, because "لُوط" is one of the foreign (aʿjamī) names, not Arabic. As for "لِطْتُ الحَوْضَ", and "this is more attached (ألْوَطُ) to my heart than that", meaning "closer (ألْصَقُ) to my heart", and "اَللِّيطُ" meaning the peel — this is correct in the language, but the name is foreign, like "إبْراهِيمَ" and "إسْحاقَ"; we do not say that it is derived from "اَلسُّحْقُ", which is remoteness. This is the Book of Allah, whose explanation one should not venture upon except with a sound transmission and a clear proof.
And His saying: ﴿أتَأْتُونَ الفاحِشَةَ ما سَبَقَكم بِها مِن أحَدٍ مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾: this is proof that the indecency of sodomy (اللِّواط) was not committed by anyone before the people of Lot. People have differed about the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) of the sodomite. Some said he is like the fornicator; and it is related that Abū Bakr burned with fire a man called "al-Fujāʾa" for sodomy. Others said he must be killed, whether married (muḥṣan) or unmarried, because Allah — Blessed and Exalted is He — killed those who did it with stones. Lot addressed them saying: ﴿أتَأْتُونَ الفاحِشَةَ﴾, and He said elsewhere: ﴿إنَّكم لَتَأْتُونَ الفاحِشَةَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 28]. "اَلْفاحِشَةُ" is the gross, ugly thing.

zajjaj:82-82.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلا أنْ قالُوا أخْرِجُوهُمْ﴾: "جَوابَ" may be nominative: "وَما كانَ جَوابُ قَوْمِهِ إلّا أنْ قالُوا"; but the better is the accusative, and the reading is upon it.
﴿إلا أنْ قالُوا أخْرِجُوهم مِن قَرْيَتِكم إنَّهم أُناسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾, i.e. they keep themselves pure from your practice.

zajjaj:83-83.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأنْجَيْناهُ وأهْلَهُ﴾: in the exegesis [it is said] that his family were his two daughters. ﴿إلا امْرَأتَهُ كانَتْ مِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾: two views have been stated about "اَلْغابِرِينَ" here. The lexicographers said: "مِنَ الغابِرِينَ" means "of those who remained", i.e. of those remaining in the place in which they were punished. Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā recited:
؎فَما ونى مُحَمَّدٌ مُذْ أنْ غَفَرْ ∗∗∗ لَهُ الإلَهُ ما مَضى وما غَبَرْ
(Muḥammad has not slackened since God forgave him what is past and what remains.)
I.e. what remains. Some said: "مِنَ الغابِرِينَ" means of those absent from salvation. Both are valid interpretations, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإلى مَدْيَنَ أخاهم شُعَيْبًا﴾: "مَدْيَنُ" is a diptote, because it is a name for the tribe or the town; and it may be foreign.
And His saying: ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكم فَأوْفُوا الكَيْلَ والمِيزانَ﴾: one of the grammarians said: Shuʿayb had no sign except prophethood. This is a gross mistake. He said: "قَدْ جاءَتْكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكم فَأوْفُوا الكَيْلَ", bringing the fāʾ as the answer to the condition; so how could he say ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ if he had no sign except prophethood? If there was a sign along with the prophethood, then he brought it to them, and whoever said "he had no sign" erred. Were anyone to claim prophethood without a sign, it would not be accepted from him. Rather, what is to be said about Shuʿayb is that his sign — as he said — is a clear proof, except that Allah — exalted be His praise — mentioned some of the signs of the prophets in the Qurʾān, and for some of them He did not mention their sign; and of one whose sign is not mentioned it is not said "he has no sign". The signs of Muḥammad the Prophet ﷺ are not all mentioned in the Qurʾān, nor most of them.
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَبْخَسُوا النّاسَ أشْياءَهُمْ﴾: "اَلْبَخْسُ" is diminution and paucity. One says "بَخَسْتُ، أبْخَسُ" with sīn, and "بَخَصْتُ عَيْنَهُ (I gouged his eye)" with ṣād, and nothing else, like "فَقَأْتُ عَيْنَيْهِ (I put out his eyes)". ﴿وَلا تُفْسِدُوا في الأرْضِ بَعْدَ إصْلاحِها﴾, i.e. do not practise acts of disobedience in it and defrauding people, after Allah has set it right by commanding justice and sending messengers.

zajjaj:86-86.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْعُدُوا بِكُلِّ صِراطٍ تُوعِدُونَ﴾, i.e. on every road. The meaning of "تُوعِدُونَ" is: you threaten whoever believes in Shuʿayb with punishment and intimidation. One says "وَعَدْتُهُ خَيْرًا (I promised him good)" and "وَعَدْتُهُ شَرًّا (I promised him evil)"; but when you mention neither of them, you say of good "وَعَدْتُهُ" and of evil "أوْعَدْتُهُ".
And His saying: ﴿وَتَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from the path by which Allah has granted security to whoever believes in it. ﴿وَتَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا﴾, i.e. and you seek crookedness and deviation from the right course. Of religion, and of what is known [mentally], when it is not straight, one says "عِوَجٌ" with kasra on the ʿayn; and of a wall or a stick, "عَوَجٌ" with fatḥa on the ʿayn.
And His saying: ﴿واذْكُرُوا إذْ كُنْتُمْ قَلِيلا فَكَثَّرَكُمْ﴾: it is possible that "فَكَثَّرَكم" means He made you rich after you were poor; it is possible that their number was small and He multiplied them; and it is possible that they were without power and standing, and He increased them. In any case, he reminded them of the favour of Allah upon them, as He said: ﴿فاذْكُرُوا آلاءَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 74], i.e. the favours of Allah.

zajjaj:189-189.t:
Then He made clear to them what guided them to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ﴾, meaning Adam, ﴿وَجَعَلَ مِنها زَوْجَها لِيَسْكُنَ إلَيْها فَلَمّا تَغَشّاها﴾: a metonymy for intercourse, the finest of metonymies. ﴿حَمَلَتْ حَمْلا خَفِيفًا﴾ means the sperm. "اَلْحَمْلُ", with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, is what is in the womb or what a tree produces; and "اَلْحِمْلُ", with kasra on the ḥāʾ, is what is carried (a load).
His saying: ﴿فَمَرَّتْ بِهِ﴾: the meaning of "مَرَّتْ بِهِ" is: she continued with it, sitting and standing, and it did not weigh her down. ﴿فَلَمّا أثْقَلَتْ﴾ means: her delivery drew near; because at its beginning it was light, and when it was made a human being and delivery drew near, she grew heavy.
His saying: ﴿دَعَوا اللَّهَ رَبَّهُما﴾ means: Adam and Eve called upon their Lord: ﴿لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنا صالِحًا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشّاكِرِينَ﴾ ﴿فَلَمّا آتاهُما صالِحًا جَعَلا لَهُ شُرَكاءَ فِيما آتاهُما﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 190]. It is related in the exegesis that Iblīs, upon him be the curse, came to Eve and said: "Do you know what is in your womb?" She said: "I do not know." He said: "Perhaps it is a beast." Then he said: "If I call upon Allah to make it a human being, will you name it after me?" She said: "Yes." So she named it "ʿAbd al-Ḥārith", and he (Iblīs) is al-Ḥārith. This is related in the exegesis.
It was also said that Adam and Eve are the origin, and this was struck as a parable for the polytheists of the Arabs, and they were made to know how He began creation. So it was said: when Allah gave the two of them, (that is,) to every male and female to whom Allah gave a child, male or female, He being the one who created it and shaped it, ﴿جَعَلا لَهُ شُرَكاءَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 190], meaning those who worshipped idols; ﴿فَتَعالى اللَّهُ عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 190]. The first is the one on which the exegesis rests.
Whoever reads "شِرْكًا", it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "شَرِكْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أشْرِكُهُ، شِرْكًا" (I became the man's partner). Someone said: according to the reading of whoever reads "شِرْكًا", it ought to have been "جَعَلا لَغَيْرِهِ شِرْكًا" (they assigned a share to other than Him); he says: because the two of them do not deny that the origin is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so the share would only be assigned to other than Him. But this is in the sense of "جَعَلا لَهُ ذا شِرْكٍ" (they assigned Him one having a share), with "ذا" omitted, like ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82].

zajjaj:199-199.t: His saying: ﴿خُذِ العَفْوَ﴾: "اَلْعَفْوُ" is the surplus, and "اَلْعَفْوُ" is what comes without effort. ﴿وَأْمُرْ بِالعُرْفِ﴾ means: with what is right (al-maʿrūf), ﴿وَأعْرِضْ عَنِ الجاهِلِينَ﴾ (and turn away from the ignorant).

zajjaj:200-200.t: His saying: ﴿وَإمّا يَنْـزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَـزْغٌ﴾: (nazgh is used) for the slightest movement there may be; you say "قَدْ نَزَغْتُهُ" when you have stirred it. So the meaning is: "If the slightest prompting from Satan reaches you", that is, whispering.

zajjaj:201-201.t:
His saying: ﴿مَسَّهم طائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ﴾: one says "طُفْتُ، أطُوفُ" (I went round, I go round), and "طافَ الخَيالُ، يَطِيفُ" (the phantom visited, it visits).
His saying: ﴿تَذَكَّرُوا فَإذا هم مُبْصِرُونَ﴾ means: they reflected on the proof that was clearest to them, and then they saw, with insight.

zajjaj:202-202.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإخْوانُهم يَمُدُّونَهم في الغَيِّ﴾: this is meant to be placed earlier; the meaning is: "They are not able to help you, nor can they help themselves; and their brothers draw them further into error, then they do not stop short", meaning the devils, because the disbelievers are the brothers of the devils. "اَلْغَيُّ" is ignorance and falling into (ruin). One says "أقْصَرَ، يُقْصِرُ" and "قَصَّرَ، يُقَصِّرُ".
[Translator's note: the text reads "والوُقُوعُ في الحَرَكَةِ" (falling into movement), probably a corruption of "الهَلَكَةِ" (ruin); rendered accordingly with the literal wording noted here.]

zajjaj:203-203.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا لَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بِآيَةٍ﴾ (and when you do not bring them a sign, they say: why have you not ...) means: why have you not fabricated it? That is: why have you not brought it from yourself? So he ﷺ informed them that the signs come from Allah, exalted be His praise.
His saying: ﴿إنَّما أتَّبِعُ ما يُوحى إلَيَّ مِن رَبِّي هَذا بَصائِرُ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ means: this Qurʾān which I have brought is insights (baṣāʾir) from your Lord. The singular of "اَلْبَصائِرُ" is "بَصِيرَةٌ". "اَلْبَصِيرَةُ" and "اَلْبَصائِرُ" are also trails of blood; al-Asʿar al-Juʿfī said:
؎راحُوا بَصائِرُهم عَلى أكْتافِهِمْ ∗∗∗ وبَصِيرَتِي يَعْدُو بِها عَتَدٌ وأى
(They went off with their blood-trails on their shoulders, while my blood-trail is carried at a run by a sturdy, swift steed.)
And "اَلْبَصِيرَةُ" is the shield, its plural being "بَصائِرُ". All of this likewise means the appearance and clarity of a thing.

zajjaj:204-204.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا قُرِئَ القُرْآنُ فاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وأنْصِتُوا﴾: it is related that speaking during the prayer used to be permitted: a man would come in and say "How much have you prayed?", and it would be said: "We have prayed such-and-such". When ﴿فاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وأنْصِتُوا﴾ was revealed, speech in the prayer was forbidden, except for that by which one draws near to Allah, exalted be His praise, and what the jurists have mentioned, such as glorification (tasbīḥ), declaring His oneness (tahlīl), magnifying (takbīr), seeking forgiveness, and the like of the remembrance of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and asking Him for pardon.
It is also possible that ﴿فاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وأنْصِتُوا﴾ means: "act upon what is in it, and do not overstep it", because the meaning of someone's saying "سَمِعَ اللَّهُ دُعاءَكَ" (may Allah hear your prayer) is, in its interpretation, "may Allah answer your prayer", since Allah, exalted be His praise, is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

zajjaj:205-205.t: His saying: ﴿بِالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ﴾: "اَلْآصالُ" is the plural of "أُصُلٌ", and "اَلْأُصُلُ" is the plural of "أصِيلٌ"; so al-āṣāl is a plural of a plural. "اَلْآصالُ" are the evenings.

zajjaj:206-206.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ﴾: the angels are meant by it. ﴿وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ﴾: they declare Him free of every evil.
If someone says: Allah, exalted be His praise, is in every place; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّهُ في السَّماواتِ وفي الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 3]; so on what basis is it said of the angels "عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ" (with your Lord)? Its interpretation is: (it is said of) whoever is near to the mercy of Allah, and to His bounty and beneficence.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالَ المَلأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِن قَوْمِهِ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكَ يا شُعَيْبُ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَكَ مِن قَرْيَتِنا أوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ في مِلَّتِنا﴾: the meaning is: "One of the two things shall certainly happen", and you will not be left to persist in opposing us.
And His saying: ﴿قالَ أوَلَوْ كُنّا كارِهِينَ﴾, i.e. would you return us into your creed even if we detest it?
If someone says: how could they say to Shuʿayb "or you shall return to our creed", when Shuʿayb was a prophet? There are two views on it. One of them: since those who had been [formerly] on their creed associated partners [with Allah] [i.e. his followers], they said: "or you shall return to our creed". And it is permissible to say "something hateful has returned (عادَ) upon me from so-and-so" even if nothing hateful had preceded it before that; its interpretation is only: "something hateful has befallen me from him".
And His saying: ﴿وَما يَكُونُ لَنا أنْ نَعُودَ فِيها إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89]: people have differed about the interpretation of this. The interpretation most fitting to the wording is: "It is not for us to return to it unless Allah wills, because nothing happens other than what Allah wills". This is the doctrine of the people of the Sunna. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَما تَشاءُونَ إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Insān: 30]; and "اَلْمَشِيئَةُ (will)" in the language is clear and needs no interpretation.
So the meaning is: "It is not for us to return to it unless it has preceded in the knowledge and will of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — that we shall return to it". The confirmation of that is His saying: ﴿وَسِعَ رَبُّنا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89], then He said: ﴿عَلى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنا﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89], and elsewhere: ﴿وَما تَوْفِيقِي إلا بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ [Hūd: 88]. Some people said: "It is not for us to return to it unless Allah our Lord wills" means: and Allah does not will unbelief. They said: this is like your saying "I will not speak to you until the pitch turns white and the crow turns grey", while pitch does not turn white and the crow does not turn grey; they said: such is the interpretation of the verse. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is an error, because it contradicts more than a thousand places in the Qurʾān that do not admit two interpretations; and nothing comes into being except by His will and from His knowledge. Either His knowledge is originated, so He willed it as originated, or His knowledge is not originated, so He willed it as not originated. It is not possible, by the power of action creatures have been given, for them to bring into existence what is impossible, nor can what He knows will exist be impossible. The Sunna of the Messenger — peace be upon him — bears witness to that. But Allah — Blessed and Exalted is He — has hidden from creatures His knowledge concerning them and His will regarding their actions, and so He commanded them and forbade them, because the proof [against them] is established only by way of command and prohibition; and all of that proceeds according to what preceded in [His] knowledge and what [His] will decreed. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَما تَسْقُطُ مِن ورَقَةٍ إلا يَعْلَمُها﴾ [al-Anʿām: 59] — the verse. The falling of the leaf is attributed to it, yet He created it in it just as He created the leaf; and so on to the end of the verse.
And He said: ﴿يَعْلَمُ ما في أنْفُسِكم فاحْذَرُوهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 235] — what is in souls of passing thoughts, passing concern and passing resolve within them. So it is not possible that what He knows to be present in them should be non-existent, nor that what He knows to be non-existent should exist. So He warned them against opposing the outward [meaning] of His command and prohibition, because they are obliged to hear and obey the command when commanded, while they proceed according to what He knew of them — that they would choose obedience and choose disobedience; and there is no way for them to choose other than what He knew they would choose. If the matter were not as we have said, it would follow that their statement "Allah knew the acts of His servants before they came to be" was knowledge in a figurative sense, not knowledge in reality; but Allah the Exalted is knowing in reality, not figuratively — and praise be to Allah. Some people said — and this comes close after the first view —: the meaning is "It is not for us to return to it unless Allah our Lord wills", i.e. we have dissociated ourselves from the whole of your creed, so it is not for us to return to anything of it unless Allah wills some form of the piety by which you seek nearness to Allah, and commands us to do it, so that by this we would have returned. Abū Isḥāq said: what I hold — and it is, if Allah wills, the truth — is the first view, because His saying ﴿بَعْدَ إذْ نَجّانا اللَّهُ مِنها﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89] is only salvation from unbelief and acts of disobedience, not from acts of piety.
And His saying: ﴿وَسِعَ رَبُّنا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89]: "عِلْمًا" is accusative as tamyīz (specification).
And His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89]: the people of ʿUmān call the judge "اَلْفاتِحَ" and "اَلْفَتّاحَ".
It is also possible that ﴿افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89] means: make our matter manifest so that what is between us and our people is opened up and disclosed. So it is possible that by this they were asking that there descend upon their people such punishment and destruction as would make plain that the truth was with them.

zajjaj:91-91.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾: it is the violent earthquake.
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿فَأصْبَحُوا في دارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ﴾, i.e. bodies cast upon the ground, like settled ashes.

zajjaj:92-92.t:
And His saying: ﴿كَأنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيها﴾, i.e. as though they had never dwelt in it. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "اَلْمَغانِي" are the dwellings in which they stayed; one says "غَنِينا بِمَكانِ كَذا وكَذا", i.e. we dwelt in such-and-such a place. And "كَأنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيها" may mean: as though they had not dwelt, as though they had not lived in it in prosperity (مُسْتَغْنِينَ), as Ḥātim of Ṭayyiʾ said:
؎غَنِينا زَمانًا بِالتَّصَعْلُكِ والغِنى ∗∗∗ فَكُلًّا سَقاناهُ بِكَأْسَيْهِما الدَّهْرُ
(We lived a time in poverty and in wealth; Fate gave us to drink of both their cups.)
؎فَما زادَنا بَغْيًا عَلى ذِي قَرابَةٍ ∗∗∗ غِنانا ولا أزْرى بِأحْسابِنا الفَقْرُ
(Our wealth did not increase our oppression of any kinsman, nor did poverty disgrace our noble standing.)
The Arabs call the poor man "اَلصُّعْلُوكُ".

zajjaj:93-93.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلّى عَنْهُمْ﴾, i.e. when the punishment descended upon them, he turned away from them. ﴿وَقالَ يا قَوْمِ لَقَدْ أبْلَغْتُكم رِسالاتِ رَبِّي ونَصَحْتُ لَكم فَكَيْفَ آسى عَلى قَوْمٍ كافِرِينَ﴾: the meaning of "آسى" is "I grieve", i.e. how should my grief be intense? One says "أسِيتُ عَلى الشَّيْءِ، آسى، أسًى" when your grief over it is intense. The poet said:
؎وانْحَلَبَتْ عَيْناهُ مِن فَرْطِ الأسى
(And his eyes streamed with tears from excess of grief.)

zajjaj:94-94.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا في قَرْيَةٍ مِن نَبِيٍّ﴾: every city is called "قَرْيَةٌ"; it was named so only because people gather in it. One says "قَرَيْتُ الماءَ في الحَوْضِ" when I have collected the water in the basin; so it was called "قَرْيَة" because of the gathering of people in it. And Mecca is "the mother of towns (أُمُّ القُرى)", because the people of the towns make for it (يَؤُمُّونَها), i.e. head towards it.
And His saying: ﴿إلا أخَذْنا أهْلَها بِالبَأْساءِ والضَّرّاءِ﴾: it was said: "اَلْبَأْساءُ" is every hardship that befell them in their wealth, and "اَلضَّرّاءُ" is the illnesses that befell them; and it was said: "اَلضَّرّاءُ" is what befell them in their wealth, and "اَلْبَأْساءُ" is what befell them in their persons.
And His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّهم يَضَّرَّعُونَ﴾, i.e. they humble themselves; the original is "يَتَضَرَّعُونَ", and the tāʾ was assimilated into the ḍād.
